mosques.name: Masjid al-Haram
mosques.address: Al Masjid Al Haram Rd., Al Haram, Makkah Al Mukarramah
mosques.significance: The holiest site in Islam, home to the Kaaba
mosques.description: Masjid al-Haram, also known as the Grand Mosque, is the largest mosque in the world and surrounds Islam's holiest place, the Kaaba, in the city of Mecca. Muslims around the world face the Kaaba during their five daily prayers.
mosques.history: The mosque surrounds the Kaaba, the ancient house of worship believed built by Prophet Ibrahim. Expanded through the centuries—under Caliph Umar (638), Ottoman Sultan Selim II (1571), and Saudi expansions (1950s onward)—it is the focal point of Hajj and Umrah.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may not enter. Hajj visa required for pilgrimage. Dress modestly; Ihram for Hajj. Best visited during Ramadan or Hajj season for spiritual atmosphere.

mosques.name: Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
mosques.significance: Second holiest site in Islam, burial place of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
mosques.description: The Prophet's Mosque is the second-holiest site in Islam, built by Prophet Muhammad himself in 622 CE. It houses the tomb of the Prophet and is one of the largest mosques in the world with its iconic green dome.
mosques.architecturalStyle: Classical Islamic with Ottoman and Modern elements
mosques.history: Built by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in 622 CE after the Hijrah. The green dome marks the Prophet's burial place. Successively expanded by Umayyads, Abbasids, Mamluks, Ottomans, and Saudi rulers.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may not enter. Visitors need valid visa. Women pray in designated areas. The Rawdah (green carpet area) is highly sought—visit early morning for shorter queues.

mosques.name: Al-Aqsa Mosque
mosques.significance: Third holiest site in Islam, destination of the Prophet's night journey
mosques.description: Al-Aqsa Mosque, meaning 'The Farthest Mosque', is located in the Old City of Jerusalem. It is the third-holiest site in Islam and was the original qibla (direction of prayer) before Mecca. The compound includes both the silver-domed Al-Aqsa mosque and the Dome of the Rock.
mosques.history: Construction began under Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik (685 CE); completed by his son al-Walid I (705 CE). The Dome of the Rock enshrines the Foundation Stone. Al-Aqsa mosque lies south.
mosques.architectureNotes: Early Islamic architecture with Byzantine and Persian influences. Gold dome, blue and turquoise tilework, marble columns.
mosques.tourismNotes: Check current access and security. Modest dress required. Non-Muslims may visit the compound at designated times.

mosques.name: Imam Reza Shrine
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosque complexes by area, shrine of Imam Reza
mosques.description: The Imam Reza Shrine is a complex containing the mausoleum of Imam Reza, the eighth Imam of Twelver Shia. It is the largest mosque in the world by dimension and the second most visited religious site in the world.
mosques.history: The shrine of Imam Reza, the eighth Imam of Twelver Shia Islam, was established in 818 CE after his martyrdom. The complex grew under Samanids, Safavids, and Qajars.
mosques.architectureNotes: Persian-Islamic style with turquoise domes, golden minarets, and intricate tilework (kashi-kari).
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may visit most areas. Dress modestly; women need chador (provided). Peak pilgrimage during Nowruz and Ramadan.

mosques.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
mosques.address: Sheikh Rashid Bin Saeed St., Khor al Maqta
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in the world, architectural masterpiece
mosques.description: The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque is one of the most beautiful mosques in the world, featuring 82 domes, over 1,000 columns, and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet. It's open to visitors of all faiths.
mosques.history: Commissioned by Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, founder of the UAE. Completed in December 2007 after 11 years of construction. It honors Islamic and global cultures.
mosques.architectureNotes: 82 domes, 1,000+ columns, 24-carat gold chandeliers, and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet. White marble and semi-precious stone inlays.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required; abayas provided for women. Best time: morning. Photography allowed. Closed Friday morning.

mosques.name: Hassan II Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Africa, built on the Atlantic Ocean
mosques.description: Hassan II Mosque stands partially over the Atlantic Ocean, with a retractable roof and the world's tallest minaret at 210 meters. It's a masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship and one of the few mosques open to non-Muslims.
mosques.history: Built to commemorate King Hassan II's 60th birthday. Construction 1986–1993. Designed by French architect Michel Pinseau. Minaret at 210 m is the world's tallest.
mosques.architectureNotes: Traditional Moroccan zellige tilework, carved wood, and plaster. Retractable roof over the main prayer hall.
mosques.tourismNotes: Guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required. Tours run several times daily.

mosques.name: Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed)
mosques.address: Binbirdirek, At Meydani Cd No:10, Sultanahmet
mosques.significance: Iconic Ottoman mosque, known for its blue tiles
mosques.description: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, popularly known as the Blue Mosque, is famous for its hand-painted blue tiles adorning its interior. With six minarets and a magnificent dome, it's one of Istanbul's most iconic landmarks.
mosques.history: Built 1609–1616 by Sultan Ahmed I. Architect Sedefkar Mehmed Agha drew on Hagia Sophia and Mimar Sinan. Six minarets caused controversy; Sultan funded a seventh at Mecca.
mosques.architectureNotes: Famous for 20,000+ hand-painted blue Iznik tiles. Central dome 43 m high. Six minarets. Classic Ottoman layout.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free entry. Closed during prayer times. Modest dress; scarves and robes provided. Opposite Hagia Sophia in Sultanahmet.

mosques.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
mosques.address: Süleymaniye Mh., Prof. Sıddık Sami Onar Cd. No:1, Fatih
mosques.significance: Mimar Sinan's masterpiece, largest Ottoman-era mosque in Istanbul
mosques.description: The Süleymaniye Mosque was commissioned by Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent and designed by the legendary architect Mimar Sinan. Completed in 1557, it is considered Sinan's masterpiece and the largest Ottoman-era mosque in Istanbul. The complex includes madrasas, a hospital, a library, and the tombs of Suleiman and his wife Hürrem Sultan (Roxelana).
mosques.architectureNotes: Central dome 53m high, 26.5m diameter. Four minarets. Rivaled Hagia Sophia. Complex includes 7 madrasas, hamam, caravanserai.
mosques.history: Built 1550-1557 by Mimar Sinan for Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. Over 3,500 workers. Sinan's 'apprentice work' before Selimiye. Survived fires and earthquakes. UNESCO World Heritage as part of Historic Areas of Istanbul.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free entry. Open to visitors outside prayer times. Modest dress required. Near Grand Bazaar. Panoramic Golden Horn views.

mosques.name: Selimiye Mosque
mosques.address: Meydan Mh., Mimar Sinan Cd., Edirne
mosques.significance: Mimar Sinan's self-proclaimed masterpiece, UNESCO World Heritage Site
mosques.description: The Selimiye Mosque in Edirne was built by Mimar Sinan at age 80 for Sultan Selim II. Sinan considered it his masterpiece ('journeyman's work'), surpassing the Hagia Sophia with its 31.3m diameter dome. Its four slender minarets each have three balconies. UNESCO World Heritage since 2011.
mosques.architectureNotes: Dome 31.3m diameter, 43m high—larger than Hagia Sophia's. Four slender minarets 71m tall. Eight pillars support the dome. Exceptional Iznik tiles.
mosques.history: Built 1568-1575 by Mimar Sinan for Sultan Selim II. Sinan completed it at age 85. He called it his 'masterwork' (journeyman piece). UNESCO inscription 2011 as 'apex of Ottoman architecture'.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free entry. Open to visitors outside prayer. Modest dress required. 3 hours from Istanbul by car. Combine with Edirne historic tour.

mosques.name: Rüstem Pasha Mosque
mosques.significance: Famous for exceptional Iznik tile work, Mimar Sinan design
mosques.description: The Rüstem Pasha Mosque was designed by Mimar Sinan for Rüstem Pasha, Grand Vizier and son-in-law of Suleiman the Magnificent. Built on a terrace above shops, it is celebrated for having the finest collection of Iznik tiles of any Ottoman mosque, covering nearly every surface.
mosques.architectureNotes: Famous for extensive Iznik tilework—tulips, carnations, pomegranates. Built on raised terrace above shops. Single dome 15m diameter.
mosques.history: Built 1561-1563 by Mimar Sinan. Commissioned by Rüstem Pasha (d. 1561), Grand Vizier and husband of Mihrimah Sultan. Raised platform design due to commercial district location.
mosques.tourismNotes: Near Spice Bazaar. Free entry. Narrow stairs to reach. Best Iznik tiles in Istanbul. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Mihrimah Sultan Mosque (Üsküdar)
mosques.significance: Early Mimar Sinan work, built for Suleiman's daughter
mosques.description: The Mihrimah Sultan Mosque at Üsküdar was designed by Mimar Sinan for Princess Mihrimah, daughter of Suleiman the Magnificent. Located at the Asian shore ferry landing, it was Sinan's first major commission and demonstrates his early mastery of classical Ottoman style.
mosques.architectureNotes: Single dome, one minaret. Waterfront location. Sinan's earliest imperial mosque. Twin to Mihrimah at Edirnekapı.
mosques.history: Built 1543-1548 by Mimar Sinan. Commissioned by Mihrimah Sultan (1522-1578), favorite daughter of Suleiman. Legend says Sinan was in love with her.
mosques.tourismNotes: At Üsküdar ferry landing on Asian side. Free entry. Combine with Üsküdar walking tour. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Yeni Mosque (New Mosque)
mosques.significance: Major Ottoman imperial mosque, adjacent to Spice Bazaar
mosques.description: The Yeni Mosque (New Mosque or Valide Sultan Mosque) is a prominent imperial mosque at Eminönü. Construction began in 1597 by Safiye Sultan but was completed in 1665 by Turhan Hatice Sultan, mother of Mehmed IV. The adjacent Egyptian Bazaar was built to fund the mosque.
mosques.architectureNotes: Modeled on Şehzade Mosque. Central dome 17.5m. Two minarets with three balconies. Blue and white Iznik tiles. Royal pavilion with private entrance.
mosques.history: Started 1597 by Safiye Sultan, halted due to political events. Completed 1665 by Turhan Hatice Sultan. Took 66 years. Adjacent Egyptian Bazaar funded the complex.
mosques.tourismNotes: At Eminönü waterfront. Free entry. Combine with Spice Bazaar and Galata Bridge. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Wazir Khan Mosque
mosques.significance: Finest example of Mughal-era tile work, 'Jewel of Lahore'
mosques.description: The Wazir Khan Mosque is considered the most ornately decorated Mughal-era mosque. Built in 1634-1641 by Hakim Ilm-ud-Din Ansari (Wazir Khan), physician to Shah Jahan, it features spectacular faience tile mosaics (kashi-kari), frescoes, and calligraphy. Called the 'Jewel of Lahore'.
mosques.architectureNotes: Famous for kashi-kari (tile mosaic) work. Persian and floral patterns. Five-arch facade. Four corner minarets. Brick and tile construction.
mosques.history: Built 1634-1641 during Shah Jahan's reign. Commissioned by Hakim Ilm-ud-Din Ansari, court physician who became Governor of Lahore. Restored by Aga Khan Trust 2009-2015.
mosques.tourismNotes: In Walled City near Delhi Gate. Undergoing UNESCO-backed restoration. Combine with Lahore Fort tour. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Moti Masjid (Lahore Fort)
mosques.significance: Pearl Mosque, private royal mosque of Shah Jahan
mosques.description: Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) within Lahore Fort was built by Shah Jahan for his personal use. The small but exquisite mosque is constructed entirely of white marble. Its name comes from its lustrous white appearance, shining like a pearl.
mosques.architectureNotes: Pure white marble. Three domes with lotus finials. Five-arch facade. Private royal mosque. Small but exquisite craftsmanship.
mosques.history: Built 1630-1645 by Shah Jahan. Private mosque for royal use within Lahore Fort. Part of UNESCO World Heritage Site (Lahore Fort complex).
mosques.tourismNotes: Inside Lahore Fort (UNESCO site). Separate ticket with Fort entry. Best combined with Lahore Fort and Badshahi Mosque tour.

mosques.name: Moti Masjid (Agra Fort)
mosques.significance: Pearl Mosque of Shah Jahan, architectural gem
mosques.description: The Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) at Agra Fort was built by Shah Jahan for his personal devotions. Made entirely of white marble, it is considered one of the purest and most elegant examples of Mughal architecture. Three bulbous domes and a harmonious courtyard.
mosques.architectureNotes: Pure white marble throughout. Three domes. Seven-bay prayer hall. Minimal decoration emphasizing marble beauty. Shah Jahan's private mosque.
mosques.history: Built 1647-1655 by Shah Jahan within Agra Fort. Private royal mosque. Part of Agra Fort UNESCO World Heritage Site.
mosques.tourismNotes: Inside Agra Fort (UNESCO). Access with Agra Fort ticket. Near Diwan-i-Am and Jahangir Palace. Combine with Taj Mahal visit.

mosques.name: Faisal Mosque
mosques.significance: National mosque of Pakistan, unique tent-like design
mosques.description: Faisal Mosque is the national mosque of Pakistan, located at the foot of Margalla Hills. Its unique design resembles a desert Bedouin tent, blending contemporary architecture with traditional Islamic elements.
mosques.history: Funded by King Faisal of Saudi Arabia ($28M original donation). Designed by Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay. Construction 1976-1986. Named after King Faisal after his assassination.
mosques.architectureNotes: Tent-shaped design without traditional dome. 88m minarets (tallest in South Asia). White marble. Main hall with 8-sided shell roof.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Located at foot of Margalla Hills. Large courtyards. Educational facilities.

mosques.name: Istiqlal Mosque
mosques.address: Jl. Taman Wijaya Kusuma, Central Jakarta
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Southeast Asia, symbol of Indonesian independence
mosques.description: Istiqlal Mosque is the national mosque of Indonesia and the largest mosque in Southeast Asia. Its name means 'Independence' in Arabic, commemorating Indonesian independence. It features interfaith dialogue, standing across from Jakarta Cathedral.

mosques.name: Grand Jamia Mosque
mosques.significance: Among the world's largest mosques by capacity, Pakistan's largest
mosques.description: The Grand Jamia Mosque in Bahria Town Karachi is one of the world's largest mosques by capacity. Its design is inspired by the Selimiye Mosque in Turkey, featuring stunning Ottoman architecture with modern amenities.

mosques.name: Badshahi Mosque
mosques.address: Walled City, near Alamgiri Gate of Lahore Fort
mosques.significance: Iconic Mughal-era mosque, one of Pakistan's most visited landmarks
mosques.description: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Emperor Aurangzeb in 1673. It is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture and was the largest mosque in the world for over 300 years. Its red sandstone and marble make it one of Lahore's most iconic sights. Courtyard 161.5 × 160.6 m.
mosques.history: Built by Emperor Aurangzeb in 1673. The largest mosque in the world for over 300 years until Faisal Mosque (1986).
mosques.architectureNotes: Red sandstone and marble. Symmetrical courtyard, octagonal minarets, Persian calligraphy.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Modest dress required. Located near Lahore Fort. Best in morning light.

mosques.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
facilities: One of world's largest chandeliers and carpets
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Oman, open to non-Muslim visitors
mosques.description: The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque was completed in 2001 and can hold 20,000 worshippers. It features one of the world's largest hand-loomed carpets and a massive Swarovski crystal chandelier. Non-Muslims are welcome outside prayer times.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome outside prayer times. Modest dress required; abayas provided. One of world's largest chandeliers and carpets.

mosques.name: Putra Mosque
mosques.significance: Iconic pink-domed mosque and Putrajaya landmark
mosques.description: The Putra Mosque is known for its distinctive rose-tinted granite and stunning location on Putrajaya Lake. Completed in 1999, it combines Malay and Persian design and is one of Malaysia's most photographed mosques.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitor access. Rose-tinted granite. Waterfront location on Putrajaya Lake. Photography allowed.

mosques.name: Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddin Mosque
mosques.significance: National symbol of Brunei, one of Asia's most beautiful mosques
mosques.description: Built in 1958, this mosque stands in an artificial lagoon and is crowned by a golden dome. It blends Mughal and Malay styles and is one of the most photographed religious buildings in Southeast Asia.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitor viewing. Stands in artificial lagoon. Golden dome. One of Southeast Asia's most photographed mosques.

mosques.name: Baitul Mukarram
mosques.significance: National mosque of Bangladesh
mosques.description: Baitul Mukarram is the national mosque of Bangladesh, completed in 1968. Its design avoids the traditional dome and instead uses a contemporary interpretation of the Kaaba, making it distinctive among modern mosques.

mosques.name: Taj-ul-Masajid
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in India
mosques.description: Taj-ul-Masajid means 'Crown of Mosques.' Construction began in the 19th century and was completed in 1985. Its pink facade and vast courtyard make it one of the largest and most striking mosques in India.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
mosques.significance: Largest adobe building in the world, UNESCO World Heritage Site
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Djenné is the largest mud-brick (adobe) building in the world. Rebuilt in 1907, it is a pinnacle of Sudano-Sahelian architecture and is replastered annually by the community. UNESCO World Heritage since 1988.
mosques.history: Rebuilt in 1907. UNESCO World Heritage since 1988. Largest adobe building in the world. Replastered annually by the community during the Crepissage festival.
mosques.architectureNotes: Sudano-Sahelian style. Mud bricks, wooden beams (toron) protruding from walls. Three minarets.
mosques.tourismNotes: Interior access for non-Muslims is limited. Best viewed from outside during the annual replastering festival.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Kuwait
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Kuwait
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Kuwait was completed in 1986 and can accommodate over 11,000 worshippers. It houses a large Islamic library and is known for its elegant design and one of Kuwait's largest prayer carpets.

mosques.name: Jama Masjid
mosques.address: Meena Bazaar, Chandni Chowk, Old Delhi
mosques.significance: India's largest mosque, Mughal architectural masterpiece
mosques.description: Jama Masjid in Old Delhi was commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan and completed in 1656. Built of red sandstone and white marble, it features three domes and two 40-meter minarets. The courtyard can hold 25,000 worshippers.
mosques.history: Built by Shah Jahan 1644–1656. Same emperor as the Taj Mahal. The mosque faces west toward Mecca.
mosques.architectureNotes: Red sandstone and white marble. Three domes, two minarets. Symmetrical courtyard. Persian and Indian influences.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Modest dress required; robes provided. Climb minaret for city views. Closed during prayer. Near Chandni Chowk.

mosques.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the world's oldest universities, center of Islamic learning
mosques.description: Al-Azhar Mosque was founded in 970 CE by the Fatimid Caliphate. It houses Al-Azhar University, one of the world's oldest degree-granting universities. A center of Sunni Islamic scholarship for over a millennium.
mosques.history: Founded 970 CE by Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz. Al-Azhar University established 988. Expanded by Mamluks and Ottomans. Major center of Islamic scholarship.
mosques.architectureNotes: Fatimid foundation with Mamluk and Ottoman additions. Multiple minarets from different eras. Marble, stucco, wood carvings.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may visit. Modest dress required. Near Khan el-Khalili bazaar. Combine with Islamic Cairo tour.

mosques.name: Islamic Center of Washington
mosques.significance: First major mosque in Washington D.C., diplomatic and cultural landmark
mosques.description: The Islamic Center of Washington was dedicated in 1957. Designed by Italian architect Mario Rossi, it blends traditional Islamic architecture with modern elements. Serves the diplomatic community and visitors from around the world.
mosques.history: Founded by Muslim diplomats. Dedicated 1957. President Eisenhower attended. Designed by Mario Rossi in Mamluk style.
mosques.architectureNotes: Mamluk-inspired. Minaret 50 m. Persian carpets, Turkish tiles, Egyptian woodwork. Stained glass.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome. Modest dress required; abayas provided. Near Embassy Row. Free tours.

mosques.name: Imam Ali Shrine
mosques.significance: One of Shia Islam's holiest sites, tomb of Imam Ali
mosques.description: The Imam Ali Shrine in Najaf is the burial place of Imam Ali, the fourth Caliph and first Imam of Shia Islam. One of the world's largest mosque complexes by capacity and area, it attracts millions of pilgrims annually.
mosques.history: The shrine was established in 977 CE. Rebuilt and expanded many times. The golden dome and minarets were added in Ottoman and Qajar eras. A major center of Shia scholarship.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may visit. Modest dress required; abayas provided for women. Check travel advisories before visiting.

mosques.name: National Mosque of Malaysia
mosques.significance: National mosque of Malaysia, modernist Islamic architecture
mosques.description: The National Mosque of Malaysia was completed in 1965. Its distinctive folded plate roof and 73-meter minaret make it a landmark of Kuala Lumpur. Designed by a team of three architects in a modernist Islamic style.
mosques.history: Built to commemorate Malaysian independence (1957). Completed 1965. Named Masjid Negara.
mosques.architectureNotes: Folded plate concrete roof instead of traditional dome. 73 m minaret. Capacity 15,000.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome outside prayer times. Modest dress required; robes provided. Near Lake Gardens and KL Bird Park.

mosques.name: Djamaa el Djazaïr
mosques.significance: Africa's largest mosque, world's third-largest mosque
mosques.description: Djamaa el Djazaïr, also known as the Great Mosque of Algiers, was completed in 2019. It features the world's tallest minaret at 265 meters and is the largest mosque in Africa.
mosques.history: Construction 2012–2019. Designed by KSP Jürgen Engel Architekten. World's tallest minaret (265 m).
mosques.architectureNotes: Contemporary design with traditional elements. 265 m minaret. Interior space 20,000 m². Seismic-resistant.
mosques.tourismNotes: Guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required. Located on the Bay of Algiers.

mosques.name: Birmingham Central Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the UK's largest and oldest purpose-built mosques
mosques.description: Birmingham Central Mosque opened in 1975 and serves one of the UK's largest Muslim communities. Its golden dome and minarets are a prominent landmark in the city.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome. Modest dress required. Contact for tour arrangements.

mosques.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
mosques.address: Süleymaniye Mah., Prof. Sıddık Sami Onar Cad. No:1, Fatih
mosques.significance: Masterpiece of Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan, imperial mosque
mosques.description: The Süleymaniye Mosque was built by Mimar Sinan for Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent and completed in 1557. Perched on one of Istanbul's seven hills, it dominates the skyline and is considered Sinan's greatest work.
mosques.history: Built 1550–1557 by Mimar Sinan for Sultan Süleyman. The complex includes tombs of Süleyman and his wife Hürrem Sultan (Roxelana). Damaged by fire in 1660, restored.
mosques.architectureNotes: Four minarets (ten balconies total). Central dome 53 m high. Courtyard with ablution fountain. Ottoman classical layout.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free entry. Modest dress required. Closed during prayer. Located in Fatih, near Grand Bazaar.

mosques.name: National Mosque
mosques.significance: National mosque of Nigeria, landmark of Abuja
mosques.description: The National Mosque in Abuja was completed in 1984 and serves as the national mosque of Nigeria. Its golden domes and minarets are a prominent landmark in the capital city.
mosques.history: Completed 1984. Designed by AIM Consultants. National mosque of Nigeria, located near the National Christian Centre.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome. Modest dress required. Contact for tour arrangements.

mosques.name: Abdul Rahman Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Afghanistan, central Kabul landmark
mosques.description: The Abdul Rahman Mosque, also known as the Grand Mosque of Kabul, is one of Afghanistan's largest mosques. Built on 1.4 hectares in the heart of Kabul, it features 19 domes, two minarets, and a three-story prayer hall with a dedicated women's floor.
mosques.history: Construction began in 2001 by businessman Hajji Abdul Rahman. Major work completed in 2009; officially inaugurated July 2012 by President Karzai.
mosques.architectureNotes: 19 domes, 2 minarets, 44 arched windows around the main dome. Prayer hall 56×24 m with three floors.

mosques.name: King Abdullah I Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Amman, only mosque in the city open to non-Muslim visitors
mosques.description: The King Abdullah I Mosque was built as a memorial to Jordan's founding king. Its distinctive blue mosaic dome dominates the Abdali skyline. The only mosque in Amman that openly welcomes non-Muslim visitors.
mosques.history: Built 1982–1989 by King Hussein as a memorial to his grandfather King Abdullah I. Octagonal prayer hall with no interior pillars.
mosques.architectureNotes: Blue mosaic dome 35 m diameter, 31 m high. Main hall holds 3,000; courtyard 3,000; women's section 500.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome. Modest dress required; abayas and headscarves provided free. Islamic Museum inside.

mosques.name: Imam Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab Mosque
mosques.arabicName: جامع الإمام محمد بن عبد الوهاب
facilities: Separate ablution halls for men and women
mosques.significance: Qatar's largest mosque, national grand mosque
mosques.description: The Imam Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab Mosque, also known as Qatar State Grand Mosque, is Qatar's largest mosque. It features 93 domes—28 large domes over the central hall—and accommodates over 30,000 worshippers.
mosques.history: Refurbishment and expansion began December 2006; inaugurated 2011. Named after the 18th-century Islamic scholar.
mosques.architectureNotes: 28 large domes, 65 smaller domes. Sandstone facades. Central hall air-conditioned for 10,000+ men; 1,300 women in separate areas.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to all visitors during non-prayer times. Modest dress required; scarves and abayas provided. Photography prohibited in ladies' area.

mosques.name: Al-Fateh Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Bahrain, national mosque
mosques.description: The Al-Fateh Grand Mosque is Bahrain's largest mosque, named after Ahmed Al-Fateh, the founder of Bahrain. It features one of the world's largest fiberglass domes and Italian marble throughout.
mosques.history: Opened in 1988. Serves as place of worship and educational center. One of the largest fiberglass domes in the world.
mosques.architectureNotes: Italian marble flooring, teakwood doors from India, ornate chandeliers. Large fiberglass dome.
mosques.tourismNotes: Guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required; abayas provided. Near Bahrain National Museum.

mosques.name: Massalikoul Djinane Mosque
mosques.significance: West Africa's largest mosque, commemorates Sheikh Ahmadou Bamba
mosques.description: Massalikoul Djinane is West Africa's largest mosque, inaugurated in 2019. Built to commemorate Sheikh Ahmadou Bamba, founder of the Mouride Brotherhood, it features five minarets, Carrara marble, and a chandelier with 2,000 lights.
mosques.architecturalStyle: Contemporary Islamic with West African influences
mosques.history: Construction took over 15 years. Inaugurated September 27, 2019. Built to commemorate Sheikh Ahmadou Bamba. 75 m height; minaret pinnacle 80 m.
mosques.architectureNotes: Five minarets, Carrara marble, golden columns. 10,000 in prayer hall; 20,000 on esplanade.
mosques.tourismNotes: Guided tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required. West Africa's grandest mosque.

mosques.name: Heydar Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Azerbaijan and the Caucasus region
mosques.description: Heydar Mosque is the largest mosque in Azerbaijan and the Caucasus. Completed in 2014, it features four 95-meter minarets and a 55-meter main dome. The complex can accommodate 75,000 worshippers.
mosques.history: Construction began September 2012; opened December 26, 2014. Designed by Ədalət Məmmədov. Named after former President Heydar Aliyev.
mosques.architectureNotes: Four minarets 95 m high. Main dome 55 m; second dome 35 m. Interior area 4,200 m².

mosques.name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
mosques.significance: Downtown Beirut's iconic Blue Mosque, largest Sunni mosque in Lebanon
mosques.description: The Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque, known as the Blue Mosque for its light blue tiles, dominates downtown Beirut near Martyrs Square. Commissioned by former Prime Minister Rafic Hariri, it was inaugurated in 2008.
mosques.history: Construction began 2002 following donation by PM Rafic Hariri. Inaugurated 2008. Hariri buried adjacent in Martyrs Square. Damaged in 2020 Beirut explosion but structure intact.
mosques.architectureNotes: Five blue-tiled domes, 48 m main dome, four minarets 65 m. Designed by Azmi Fakhoury.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome. Modest dress required. Near Martyrs Square and Mohammad Al-Amin Square.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Khartoum
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Sudan, historic Turkish-Islamic style
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Khartoum, also known as Al Kabir Mosque, is Sudan's largest mosque. Built in Turkish-Islamic style with reddish sandstone, it was opened in 1901 and accommodates up to 10,000 worshippers.
mosques.history: Built 1900; officially opened 1901 when Khedive Abbas II of Egypt visited during Anglo-Egyptian Sudan. Center of old Khartoum.

mosques.name: Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest historical mosque in Bosnia, representative Ottoman structure in the Balkans
mosques.description: The Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque, built in 1530, is the largest historical mosque in Bosnia and Herzegovina. A masterpiece of Early Ottoman architecture, it was the first mosque in the world to receive electric illumination in 1898.
mosques.history: Built 1530 as part of Gazi Husrev-beg's endowment (madrasa, marketplace, hammam). First mosque with electricity 1898. Restored after Bosnian War.
mosques.architectureNotes: Central dome 13 m diameter, 26 m high. Minaret ~36 m. Five marble columns, portico with five cupolas. Cut stone construction.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome outside prayer. Modest dress required. In Baščaršija, heart of old Sarajevo.

mosques.name: Hazrat Sultan Mosque
mosques.annualVisitors: Second largest mosque in Central Asia
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Kazakhstan, second largest in Central Asia
mosques.description: Hazrat Sultan Mosque opened in 2012 and is Kazakhstan's largest mosque. Its 51-meter dome and four 77-meter minarets dominate the Astana skyline. The complex covers over 11 hectares.
mosques.history: Opened July 6, 2012. Built in classical Islamic style. Second largest in Central Asia after Turkmenbashi Ruhy.
mosques.architectureNotes: Dome 51 m high, 28.1 m base diameter. Four minarets 77 m. Construction area 17,700 m².
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors welcome. Modest dress required. Near Bayterek Tower and Khan Shatyr.

mosques.name: Al-Zaytuna Mosque
mosques.significance: Oldest mosque in Tunis, hosted one of Islam's first universities
mosques.description: Al-Zaytuna Mosque, the Mosque of the Olive, is the oldest mosque in Tunis and hosted the University of Ez-Zitouna—one of the first and greatest universities in Islamic history. Its 160 columns were brought from the ruins of Carthage.
mosques.history: Founded c. 698–732 CE. Modeled on Great Mosque of Kairouan. University of Ez-Zitouna established. Scholars included Ibn Khaldun, Ibn 'Arafa.
mosques.architectureNotes: Prayer room 56×24 m (1,344 m²). Minaret 43 m. Trapezoidal courtyard, columns with marble capitals.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may visit. Modest dress required. In medina of Tunis, near souks.

mosques.name: Astana Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in Central Asia, serving as a major religious landmark in Kazakhstan's capital.
mosques.description: Astana Grand Mosque is a newly built mosque complex with a vast prayer hall, courtyards, and facilities for religious education and community activities.

mosques.name: Jamkaran Mosque
mosques.significance: A major Shia pilgrimage mosque near Qom associated with traditions about the Mahdi.
mosques.description: Jamkaran Mosque is a large mosque complex on the outskirts of Qom, frequently visited by pilgrims and known for its spacious courtyards and prayer halls.

mosques.name: Egypt's Islamic Cultural Center (Masjid Misr Al Kabeer)
mosques.significance: A new flagship mosque and Islamic cultural complex in Egypt's New Administrative Capital.
mosques.description: Masjid Misr Al Kabeer is a large contemporary mosque integrated into Egypt's Islamic Cultural Center, designed to host major religious events and educational programs.

mosques.name: Umayyad Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the oldest and most historically significant mosques in the world.
mosques.description: The Umayyad Mosque in Damascus is a major early Islamic monument known for its large courtyard, prayer hall, and rich historical associations.

mosques.name: Bahria Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: A large congregational mosque serving the Bahria Town Lahore development.
mosques.description: Bahria Grand Mosque is a modern mosque complex with multiple domes and large interior spaces built to serve residents of Bahria Town Lahore.

mosques.name: Çamlıca Mosque
mosques.significance: A major contemporary mosque complex on Çamlıca Hill overlooking Istanbul.
mosques.description: Çamlıca Mosque is a large hilltop mosque in Istanbul that combines traditional Ottoman-inspired elements with modern amenities and extensive public spaces.

mosques.name: Al Jabbar Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in West Java, landmark 'floating mosque' designed by Governor Ridwan Kamil
mosques.description: Al-Jabbar Grand Mosque (Masjid Raya Al Jabbar) is a neo-futuristic mosque on the Gedebage reservoir in Bandung. Designed by Governor Ridwan Kamil, it combines Ottoman, Sundanese, and modern styles. Opened December 2022 after five years of construction costing ~$64 million.
mosques.architectureNotes: Main dome without central pillar. Four 99-meter minarets. Floating appearance over reservoir. Geometric latticework (mashrabiya). White and gold palette.
mosques.history: Groundbreaking December 29, 2017. Opened December 30, 2022. Designed by Ridwan Kamil when he was mayor of Bandung. Built on remnants of ancient Bandung Lake.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Observation deck on minarets. Part of West Java's tourism promotion. Near Gedebage area.

mosques.name: Jameh Mosque of Makki
mosques.significance: Largest Sunni Friday mosque in Iran, one of world's largest Hanafi mosques
mosques.description: The Jameh Mosque of Makki (Grand Makki Mosque of Zahedan) is the largest Sunni mosque in Iran and one of the world's largest Hanafi mosques. Founded in 1971 by Abdul Aziz Malazada, it serves the Baloch Sunni community. Led by Molavi Abdolhamid, it is a center of Sunni religious life in southeastern Iran.
mosques.architectureNotes: Ottoman-influenced design. Large prayer hall capacity 60,000. Part of Jamiat Darul Uloom seminary complex. Expanded c. 2010.
mosques.history: Founded 1971 by Abdul Aziz Malazada as part of Jamiat Darul Uloom seminary. Expanded c. 2010. Center of Sunni religious authority for Baloch community in Iran.
mosques.tourismNotes: Active mosque. Visitors should check local conditions. Center of Sunni community life in Zahedan.

mosques.name: Al-Akbar Mosque
mosques.address: Jl. Masjid Al-Akbar Timur No.1, Pagesangan, Surabaya
mosques.significance: One of Indonesia's largest mosques, landmark of Surabaya with 99-meter minaret
mosques.description: Masjid Nasional Al-Akbar (National Al-Akbar Mosque) is one of Indonesia's largest mosques, inaugurated in 2000. Known for its striking turquoise-blue dome and 99-meter minaret inspired by the 99 names of Allah. The minaret offers panoramic views of Surabaya.
mosques.architectureNotes: Vibrant turquoise-blue dome. 99-meter minaret. Combines global Islamic influences with Indonesian elements. Large courtyard and gardens.
mosques.history: Inaugurated 2000. Built to symbolize Surabaya's role as a major Indonesian city while embracing Islamic heritage.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. 99-meter minaret observation deck offers city views. Accessible by public transport. Gardens and facilities available.

mosques.name: Al Saleh Mosque
mosques.significance: A large modern mosque complex in Yemen's capital city.
mosques.description: Al Saleh Mosque in Sana'a is a sizeable mosque featuring multiple domes and extensive courtyard areas, built in the early 21st century.

mosques.name: Jamia Masjid
mosques.significance: A historic congregational mosque in the Kashmir Valley.
mosques.description: Jamia Masjid in Srinagar is a timber-rich mosque with a large courtyard and characteristic Kashmiri architecture, central to religious life in the old city.

mosques.name: Jamiul Futuh, The Indian Grand Masjid
mosques.significance: A large new congregational mosque in Kerala.
mosques.description: Jamiul Futuh, known as the Indian Grand Masjid, is a recently built mosque with extensive capacity for worshippers and community events.

mosques.name: Pride of Muslims Mosque
mosques.significance: A major mosque in the Chechen Republic, also called the Pride of Muslims.
mosques.description: The Pride of Muslims Mosque in Shali is a large white-marble mosque complex with multiple minarets and domes serving worshippers in the region.

mosques.name: 1st November of 1954 Great Mosque
mosques.significance: A large mosque in Batna named after the start date of the Algerian War of Independence.
mosques.description: The 1st November of 1954 Great Mosque in Batna is a sizeable modern mosque built to commemorate a key date in Algerian history.

mosques.name: Sabancı Central Mosque
mosques.significance: A major mosque in southern Turkey with six minarets.
mosques.description: Sabancı Central Mosque stands by the Seyhan River in Adana and features a large central dome and six slender minarets inspired by classical Ottoman mosque design.

mosques.name: At-Tin Mosque
mosques.significance: A large mosque in East Jakarta dedicated in honor of Indonesia’s first lady.
mosques.description: At-Tin Mosque is a spacious mosque complex in Jakarta with a distinctive dome and landscaped grounds used for religious and community activities.

mosques.name: CMH Masjid Jhelum
mosques.significance: A large mosque associated with the Combined Military Hospital in Jhelum Cantonment.
mosques.description: CMH Masjid Jhelum is a sizeable congregational mosque in Jhelum Cantonment, used by both military personnel and local worshippers.

mosques.name: Selahaddin Eyyubi Mosque
mosques.significance: A new large mosque named after Salah ad-Din (Saladin) in Diyarbakır.
mosques.description: Selahaddin Eyyubi Mosque is a spacious contemporary mosque complex in Diyarbakır built to host large congregations and religious events.

mosques.name: Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Mosque
mosques.significance: The state mosque of Selangor, known for its large blue dome.
mosques.description: Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Mosque in Shah Alam features a massive blue and silver dome and four tall minarets, dominating the city's skyline.
mosques.architectureNotes: Folded plate concrete roof instead of traditional dome. 73 m minaret. Capacity 15,000.
mosques.history: Built to commemorate Malaysian independence (1957). Completed 1965. Named Masjid Negara.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims welcome outside prayer times. Modest dress required; robes provided. Near Lake Gardens and KL Bird Park.

mosques.name: Jakarta Islamic Center
mosques.significance: A major Islamic educational and worship complex in Jakarta.
mosques.description: Jakarta Islamic Center is a multi-purpose complex incorporating a large mosque and facilities for Islamic education and community development.

mosques.name: Aqsa Mosque
mosques.significance: A central mosque for the Ahmadiyya community in Rabwah.
mosques.description: The Aqsa Mosque in Rabwah is a sizeable congregational mosque associated with the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community in Pakistan.

mosques.name: Dian Al-Mahri Mosque
mosques.significance: A large mosque in Depok known for its gold-colored domes.
mosques.description: Dian Al-Mahri Mosque is a popular mosque complex near Jakarta featuring golden domes and landscaped grounds that attract worshippers and visitors.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Conakry
mosques.significance: The main mosque in Guinea's capital and one of the largest in West Africa.
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Conakry is a major national mosque complex in Guinea built to host large congregations for Friday and Eid prayers.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of West Sumatra
mosques.significance: A regional landmark mosque with distinctive Minangkabau-inspired rooflines.
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of West Sumatra in Padang combines modern construction with traditional Minangkabau roof forms in a large coastal mosque complex.

mosques.name: Id Kah Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in China and a historic center of Uyghur religious life in Kashgar.
mosques.description: Id Kah Mosque in Kashgar covers 16,800 m² and can hold up to 20,000 worshippers. Built by Saqsiz Mirza c. 1442 CE (incorporating older structures from 996 CE), it is the largest mosque in China.
mosques.architectureNotes: Large courtyard, yellow façade, gate and minarets. Central to Kashgar's old city.
mosques.history: Built c. 1442 by Saqsiz Mirza; incorporates earlier structures from 996 CE. Expanded and restored over the centuries.

mosques.name: Shah Jahan Mosque
mosques.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; Mughal-era mosque in Thatta renowned for tilework and acoustics.
mosques.description: The Shah Jahan Mosque in Thatta (93 × 52 m) was built 1644–1647. It has 93 domes and exceptional brick and tile decoration; the acoustics allow the imam's voice to carry throughout.
mosques.architectureNotes: 93 domes, elaborate tilework (kashi), central courtyard 42 × 32 m. Influential Sindhi Mughal design.
mosques.history: Built 1644–1647 under Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. Named after the emperor; key example of Sindh mosque architecture.

mosques.name: Tuanku Mizan Zainal Abidin Mosque
mosques.significance: A large modern mosque in Malaysia's administrative capital, also known as the Iron Mosque.
mosques.description: Tuanku Mizan Zainal Abidin Mosque in Putrajaya is a steel-heavy mosque design with open sides and a large prayer hall facing a lakefront.

mosques.name: Raja Hamidah Great Mosque of Batam
mosques.significance: A major mosque in Batam serving local and visiting worshippers.
mosques.description: Raja Hamidah Great Mosque of Batam is a large mosque complex that accommodates congregations from across the island city and nearby regions.

mosques.name: Hagia Sophia
mosques.significance: Historic Byzantine basilica completed 537 CE; converted to mosque 1453, museum 1935, mosque again 2020.
mosques.description: Hagia Sophia in Istanbul was built as a Byzantine cathedral in 537 CE. After the Ottoman conquest it became a mosque; it was a museum from 1935 until 2020, when it was reconsecrated as a mosque. The building is famed for its massive dome and Byzantine mosaics.
mosques.architectureNotes: Pendentive dome (31 m diameter, ~56 m high). Byzantine masonry; Ottoman minarets and calligraphy added after 1453. Mosaics partially preserved.
mosques.history: Built 532–537 under Emperor Justinian I; designed by Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles. Converted to mosque after Ottoman conquest (1453); minarets and Islamic elements added. Secularized as museum 1935; redesignated as mosque 2020.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free entry. Closed during prayer times. Modest dress; head coverings provided. Visit early to avoid crowds.

mosques.name: Al-Kauthar Mosque
mosques.significance: A prominent mosque in Tawau, Sabah.
mosques.description: Al-Kauthar Mosque in Tawau is a large coastal mosque complex serving as a major place of worship in eastern Malaysia.

mosques.name: Al-Fattah al-Aleem Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the major new mosques in Egypt's New Administrative Capital.
mosques.description: Al-Fattah al-Aleem Mosque is a large modern mosque with multiple domes and minarets, built as part of Egypt’s new capital development.

mosques.name: Federal Territory Mosque
mosques.significance: A large mosque in Kuala Lumpur inspired by Ottoman and Malay styles.
mosques.description: Federal Territory Mosque is a major congregational mosque in Kuala Lumpur with multiple domes and landscaped surrounds, serving the capital’s Muslim population.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Makhachkala
mosques.significance: A major mosque in the capital of Dagestan, Russia.
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Makhachkala is a large mosque complex serving worshippers in the North Caucasus region of Russia.

mosques.name: Aqsa Mosque
mosques.significance: A central mosque for the Ahmadiyya community in Qadian.
mosques.description: The Aqsa Mosque in Qadian is an important mosque for the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community in India, with capacity for large congregations.

mosques.name: Al-Azhom Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: A large mosque in Tangerang on the outskirts of Jakarta.
mosques.description: Al-Azhom Grand Mosque in Tangerang is a spacious mosque complex with a large dome and facilities for local congregations and events.

mosques.name: Emir Abdelkader Mosque
mosques.significance: A major mosque and Islamic university complex in Constantine.
mosques.description: Emir Abdelkader Mosque in Constantine includes a large prayer hall and educational facilities, forming an important religious center in Algeria.

mosques.name: Kocatepe Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in Ankara, featuring a classical Ottoman-inspired design.
mosques.description: Kocatepe Mosque in Ankara is a large four-minaret mosque visible across the city, built in the late 20th century.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Central Java
mosques.significance: A large mosque complex in Semarang combining Javanese and Middle Eastern influences.
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Central Java (Masjid Agung Jawa Tengah) in Semarang features six hydraulic umbrellas inspired by Medina, a pyramid-style roof, and a 99 m Asmaul Husna Tower. Prayer hall 7,669 m².
mosques.architectureNotes: Pyramid-style joglo roof, six hydraulic umbrellas (inspired by Medina), 99 m Asmaul Husna Tower, 25 pillars with calligraphy.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Sabilal Muhtadin
mosques.significance: A major mosque in Banjarmasin on the island of Borneo.
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Sabilal Muhtadin is a large congregational mosque built near the Martapura River in Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan.

mosques.name: Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in the Philippines, funded partly by the Sultan of Brunei.
mosques.description: Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mosque in Cotabato City is a large mosque with multiple domes and minarets, serving Muslims in Mindanao.

mosques.name: Imperial Mosque
mosques.significance: Ottoman-era mosque built by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror, a cultural heritage monument of Kosovo.
mosques.description: The Imperial Mosque, also known as the King's Mosque or Fatih Mosque, is a 15th-century Ottoman mosque in the heart of Pristina. Built in 1461, it is one of the oldest and most significant Islamic monuments in Kosovo.
mosques.architectureNotes: Stone and brick construction, single dome, characteristic Ottoman minaret.
mosques.history: Built in 1461 under Sultan Mehmed II (the Conqueror). Designated a cultural heritage monument of Kosovo.
mosques.tourismNotes: Modest dress required. Non-Muslims may visit outside prayer times.

mosques.name: Kalon Mosque
mosques.significance: One of Central Asia's most iconic mosques, part of the Po-i Kalyan ensemble beside the Kalon Minaret.
mosques.description: The Kalon Mosque in Bukhara is a monumental 16th-century mosque facing the famous Kalon Minaret. It forms the heart of the historic Po-i Kalyan complex and is a masterpiece of Central Asian Islamic architecture.
mosques.architectureNotes: Large courtyard, blue-tiled iwan, multiple domes. Adjacent to the 47 m Kalon Minaret (1127).
mosques.history: Built in 1514 under the Shaybanids, replacing an earlier mosque destroyed by Genghis Khan. Part of UNESCO World Heritage site Historic Centre of Bukhara.
mosques.tourismNotes: Modest dress required. Part of Bukhara's historic center; combined visits with Kalon Minaret and Mir-i Arab Madrasah.

mosques.name: Et'hem Bey Mosque
mosques.significance: Historic Ottoman mosque on Tirana's main square, famed for its exterior frescoes of trees and landscapes.
mosques.description: The Et'hem Bey Mosque is an 18th–19th century Ottoman mosque in the center of Tirana. It is renowned for its detailed frescoes and was reopened for worship in 1991 after the fall of communism.
mosques.architectureNotes: Stone and brick, single dome, minaret. Exterior frescoes depicting trees, waterfalls, and bridges.
mosques.history: Construction began under Molla Bey (1789) and completed by his son Et'hem Bey in 1821. Survived communist era; reopened 1991.
mosques.tourismNotes: Modest dress required. Non-Muslims may visit outside prayer times. On Skanderbeg Square.

mosques.name: Türkmenbaşy Ruhy Mosque
mosques.address: Gypjak village, outskirts of Ashgabat, Turkmenistan
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in Central Asia and a national symbol of Turkmenistan, combining religious and political symbolism.
mosques.description: Türkmenbaşy Ruhy Mosque, located in the village of Gypjak near Ashgabat, was commissioned by former president Saparmurat Niyazov and completed in 2004 as a monumental national mosque. The complex features a large central dome, four minarets, extensive marble cladding, and inscriptions that include both Quranic verses and references to Niyazov's book Ruhnama, reflecting its dual role as a religious and state monument.
mosques.architecturalStyle: Modern Islamic with Turkmen national motifs
mosques.history: Built between 2001 and 2004 under the direction of President Saparmurat Niyazov, the mosque was dedicated as both a place of worship and a memorial to the 'Turkmenbashi' era. Its construction used extensive white marble and gold, and the complex includes Niyazov's mausoleum, making it unusual among modern mosques. Since its opening, it has served as a prominent symbol on the outskirts of Ashgabat and is often featured in representations of Turkmen national identity.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslim visitors are generally allowed in the courtyard and sometimes in the interior outside of prayer times; modest dress required. The site is a short drive from Ashgabat and often included in local city tours.

mosques.name: Sultan Mosque
mosques.annualVisitors: Hundreds of thousands of worshippers and tourists annually
mosques.significance: National monument of Singapore and one of the most important mosques for the Malay-Muslim community in Kampong Glam.
mosques.description: Sultan Mosque, or Masjid Sultan, is an iconic mosque in Singapore's Kampong Glam district, originally built in 1824 for Sultan Hussein Shah and completely rebuilt in 1932. With its large golden domes and black-rimmed onion-shaped finials, it is a focal point of Muslim religious life and Malay heritage, and was gazetted as a national monument in 1975.
mosques.architecturalStyle: Indo-Saracenic with Islamic and European influences
mosques.history: The first mosque on the site was built in 1824 with funds from the East India Company for Sultan Hussein Shah, marking the establishment of Kampong Glam as a Malay-Muslim enclave. Due to structural deterioration and growing demand, it was rebuilt between 1924 and 1932 in its present form. In 1975, the mosque was designated a national monument in recognition of its religious and cultural importance, and it continues to serve as a key religious hub and a stopover for pilgrims traveling to Mecca.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to non-Muslim visitors during set visiting hours outside prayer times; modest dress required and robes are provided. Located in a popular heritage and tourism district with many halal eateries and cultural shops nearby.

mosques.name: Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque
mosques.address: Second Cross Street, Pettah, Colombo, Sri Lanka
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands of worshippers weekly; popular city landmark for tourists
mosques.significance: One of Colombo's most recognizable religious landmarks, known as the 'Red Mosque' for its red-and-white striped façade.
mosques.description: Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque, often called the Red Mosque, is a striking two-storey mosque in the Pettah district of Colombo, famous for its red-and-white candy-striped brickwork and Indo-Saracenic architecture. Built in the early 20th century to serve the local Muslim trading community, it remains a vibrant centre of worship and an iconic part of Colombo's skyline.
mosques.architecturalStyle: Indo-Saracenic with Gothic and Neo-classical elements
mosques.history: Commissioned by the local Bohra Muslim trading community in Pettah, construction of the mosque began in 1908 and was completed in 1909 to accommodate daily and Friday prayers. Its distinctive red-and-white brick façade and pomegranate-shaped domes soon made it a navigational landmark for sailors approaching the port of Colombo. Over the years, expansions increased capacity to around several thousand worshippers for Friday prayers and Eid, while preserving the original Indo-Saracenic design.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors are welcome outside prayer times but should respect ongoing worship, dress modestly, and ask permission before photographing interior spaces. The mosque is easily accessible on foot within the busy Pettah market area and is often included in city walking tours.

mosques.name: Mustafa Pasha Mosque
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands of worshippers and heritage tourists annually
mosques.significance: A well-preserved Ottoman-era mosque overlooking Skopje's Old Bazaar and an important monument of Islamic architecture in the Balkans.
mosques.description: Mustafa Pasha Mosque is an Ottoman imperial-style mosque built in 1492 on a hill above Skopje's Old Bazaar by Çoban Mustafa Pasha, later a vizier in the court of Sultan Selim I. The complex features a single large dome over the prayer hall, a slender minaret, and a courtyard with a türbe where Mustafa Pasha's daughter is buried, making it both a religious and historic landmark.
mosques.history: Constructed in 1492 during the height of Ottoman rule in the Balkans, the mosque was endowed by Çoban Mustafa Pasha, who later became a vizier to Sultan Selim I. Remarkably, the building has remained largely unchanged since its completion, preserving its original dome, minaret, and interior decoration. A restoration funded by the Turkish government in the early 21st century helped conserve the structure and its surrounding rose garden, reinforcing its status as a key monument in Skopje's historic landscape.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors can access the mosque courtyard and, outside prayer times, the interior; modest clothing is required. Its hilltop position offers views over the Old Bazaar and central Skopje, making it a common stop on walking tours of the historic district.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Niamey
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands of worshippers weekly; major gathering place for Eid and Friday prayers
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Niamey and one of the city's most important religious and architectural landmarks.
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Niamey is a prominent Sunni mosque on Avenue de l'Islam, built in the 1970s with financial support from Libya. Recognisable by its pale façade, green-topped dome and tall minaret with 171 steps, it serves as the main venue for Friday and Eid prayers and a key symbol of Islam in Niger's capital.
mosques.history: Constructed in the 1970s, the Grand Mosque of Niamey was funded largely by Libya and completed around 1977, shortly after Niger's independence. It features a large prayer hall and separate sections for men and women, each accommodating several thousand worshippers, and a minaret with 171 steps that offers views over the city. Over time it has become a central site for national religious ceremonies and community gatherings in Niamey.
mosques.tourismNotes: Generally open to visitors outside Friday prayer; modest dress required and local guides often offer tours for a small donation. Non-Muslim visitors may be allowed inside when accompanied by a guide, and the minaret climb provides panoramic views over Niamey.

mosques.name: King Fahad Mosque
mosques.address: Box Bar Road (Wallace Cole Road), Banjul, Gambia
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands of worshippers weekly; major mosque for national events
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Banjul and one of the most prominent Islamic landmarks in The Gambia.
mosques.description: King Fahad Mosque, also known as the Great Mosque of Banjul, is the principal mosque of Gambia's capital, located on Box Bar Road near Arch 22. Built with financial assistance from Saudi Arabia and inaugurated in 1988, it can host around 6,000 worshippers and is noted for its twin octagonal minarets, open-arched entrance and modern Islamic architectural style.
mosques.history: The mosque was constructed with Saudi funding and opened in February 1988, replacing the earlier Independence Drive mosque as Banjul's main congregational mosque. Its design combines functional modern architecture with traditional Islamic elements, including a spacious prayer hall and two octagonal minarets that dominate Banjul's skyline. Since its inauguration it has served as the focal point for Friday prayers, Eid celebrations and national religious gatherings in the capital.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors outside prayer times; modest clothing is required and non-Muslim visitors are usually welcome to view the interior with respect. The mosque is centrally located and often included in city sightseeing itineraries around Banjul.

mosques.name: Grand Friday Mosque
mosques.arabicName: مسجد الجمعة الكبير (مسجد السلطان محمد ثاكرفانو الأعظم)
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands of worshippers weekly; major attraction for visitors to Malé
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in the Maldives and the main national mosque, forming part of the Islamic Centre in Malé.
mosques.description: The Grand Friday Mosque, officially Masjid-al Sultan Mohamed Thakurufaanu Al Auzam, is the principal congregational mosque in Malé and the largest in the Maldives, accommodating over 5,000 worshippers. Its striking golden dome and tall minaret dominate the capital's skyline, and the adjoining Islamic Centre hosts religious, cultural and official events.
mosques.history: Completed in 1984 as part of the Islamic Centre complex, the Grand Friday Mosque was built to serve as the main national mosque and venue for large Friday and Eid congregations. It replaced older mosques as the primary focus of Islamic life in the capital, with a design that integrates a large marble-clad prayer hall, a prominent gold dome and a freestanding minaret visible from the sea. Over time it has become both a religious centre and a key symbol of Maldivian Islamic identity for residents and visitors alike.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors are welcome outside prayer times; modest dress is required, and non-Muslims may tour the main hall when accompanied by local staff or guides. The mosque's central location near Republic Square makes it an easy stop on walking tours of Malé.

mosques.name: Grand Anwar Mosque
mosques.address: Merkato area, Arada district, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands of worshippers weekly; especially crowded on Fridays and Ramadan
mosques.significance: Oldest and largest mosque in Addis Ababa and a key religious centre for Muslims in the Ethiopian capital.
mosques.description: Grand Anwar Mosque, located near Merkato in the Arada district, is Addis Ababa's oldest and largest mosque, completed around 1922. Built initially by the Italian administration and later finished with funds from the Muslim community, it is easily recognised by its white and green façade, multiple domes and prominent minarets, and serves as a focal point for Friday and Ramadan congregations.
mosques.history: Construction of the Grand Anwar Mosque began under the Italian administration around 1922, but a funding shortfall left 16,000 birr unpaid to the contractor until the local Muslim community raised the remainder. After a brief closure due to legal disputes, the mosque reopened and gradually became the main congregational mosque in Addis Ababa, hosting large gatherings during Ramadan and Eid. Its distinctive white and green color scheme and tall minarets have made it a landmark of the Merkato area and a symbol of Ethiopia's Islamic heritage.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors should dress modestly and avoid busy Friday prayer times; the surrounding Merkato area can be very crowded. Non-Muslims may access the courtyard and sometimes the interior if they coordinate with local guides or mosque officials.

mosques.name: Jamia Mosque Nairobi
mosques.address: Banda Street, Central Business District, Nairobi, Kenya
mosques.annualVisitors: Tens of thousands of worshippers weekly; main centre for major Islamic events in Nairobi
facilities: Shops along the side of the complex
mosques.significance: Largest and most important mosque in Kenya, serving as the central mosque (Jama Masjid) of Nairobi and a major Islamic centre for East and Central Africa.
mosques.description: Jamia Mosque is a landmark mosque in Nairobi's CBD, located between Banda Street and Kigali Road, known for its three silver domes and twin minarets. Founded by Syed Maulana Abdullah Shah in 1902 and completed in its present form in 1933, it is built in a traditional Arabic-Islamic style with white façades, arched windows and marble and ceramic finishes, and functions as both a place of worship and a hub for Islamic education and outreach.
mosques.history: Jamia Mosque was founded by Syed Maulana Abdullah Shah in 1902, but legal restrictions on land ownership delayed construction of a permanent structure until 1925. The main building, inspired by Mughal mosques such as Delhi's Jama Masjid and Lahore's Badshahi Mosque, was completed in 1933 and soon became the principal congregational mosque for Nairobi and a centre for Muslim organization during the colonial and post-independence periods. Over time it has been expanded with added floors, a women's gallery, library and training facilities, while retaining its iconic three silver domes and minarets.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims are generally welcome to visit outside prayer times; shoes must be removed and women should cover their heads. The mosque is in a busy downtown area, so visits are best planned outside Friday midday prayers.

mosques.name: Abdülhamid Han II Mosque
mosques.address: Salines Ouest district, Djibouti City, Djibouti
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands of worshippers weekly; major new landmark for visitors to Djibouti City
facilities: Educational and social spaces within the complex
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Djibouti and a prominent Ottoman-style landmark built as a symbol of Turkey–Djibouti cooperation.
mosques.description: Abdülhamid Han II Mosque is a large Ottoman-style mosque built on reclaimed land in the Salines Ouest district of Djibouti City, near the presidential palace. Covering more than 13,000 square metres, it features a central dome about 27 metres high, two 46-metre minarets and interior decoration inspired by classic Turkish mosques, making it the biggest symbolic religious structure in the country.
mosques.history: Construction of the Abdülhamid Han II Mosque and complex began around 2015 under the auspices of Türkiye Diyanet Foundation, using materials and artisans from Turkey. The mosque was inaugurated in November 2019 in a ceremony attended by senior Djiboutian officials and Turkish representatives and has since become the largest and most visible Islamic architectural work in the capital. Its Ottoman-style design and strategic waterfront location underscore Djibouti's growing cultural and diplomatic ties with Turkey.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors outside prayer times; modest clothing required, and guided visits may be available as it is promoted as a city landmark. Its coastal position makes it easily combined with waterfront walks and visits to nearby civic buildings.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Bobo-Dioulasso
mosques.address: Old town of Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands of worshippers and heritage tourists annually
mosques.significance: One of the best-known examples of Sudano-Sahelian earthen mosque architecture and a major religious site in western Burkina Faso.
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Bobo-Dioulasso is a large adobe mosque in the old quarter of Bobo-Dioulasso, characterized by thick mud-brick walls, wooden toron beams and tapering minaret towers typical of Sudano-Sahelian architecture. It remains a functioning place of worship while also attracting visitors who come to explore its narrow interior spaces and rooftop views over the old town.
mosques.history: The mosque's earliest sections date from the late 19th century and were expanded in the early 20th century as Bobo-Dioulasso grew as a trade centre, resulting in the current large, multi-chambered prayer space. Its earthen construction requires periodic replastering by local masons, a process that has helped preserve traditional building techniques and community involvement in mosque upkeep. Over time it has become both a key religious institution and one of Burkina Faso's most photographed architectural landmarks.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors are typically required to hire a local guide; modest dress and removal of shoes are mandatory. Photography is usually permitted from the outside and rooftops, but interior images may require permission from mosque authorities.

mosques.name: Hukuru Miskiy (Old Friday Mosque)
mosques.address: Kaafu Atoll, Malé, Maldives (near Medhu Ziyaaraiy)
mosques.annualVisitors: Significant numbers of worshippers and heritage tourists annually
mosques.significance: One of the oldest mosques in the Maldives, famous for its coral-stone walls and intricate traditional calligraphy and woodcarving.
mosques.description: Hukuru Miskiy, also known as the Old Friday Mosque, is a 17th-century coral-stone mosque in Malé, recognised for its finely carved Quranic inscriptions and lacquered woodwork. Surrounded by a historic cemetery with elaborately carved tombstones, it is an important example of Maldivian Islamic architecture and a key heritage site alongside the newer Grand Friday Mosque.
mosques.history: The mosque was commissioned by Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar I and completed in 1658 on the site of an earlier mosque built soon after the Maldives' conversion to Islam. Its coral-stone walls are carved with Quranic text and geometric patterns, while the interior features elaborately lacquered wood panels and ceiling beams. Conservation efforts in recent decades have focused on protecting the delicate coral fabric from weathering and urban development pressures.
mosques.tourismNotes: Entry for non-Muslims may be restricted and usually requires permission from staff or a local guide; respectful dress is essential. Visitors often combine it with a stop at the nearby Islamic Centre and Grand Friday Mosque.

mosques.name: Islamic Center of America
mosques.annualVisitors: Tens of thousands annually; thousands weekly for prayers and programs
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in North America and a major Shia Islamic center serving the Lebanese-American community and wider Muslim population.
mosques.description: The Islamic Center of America in Dearborn is a 120,000-square-foot complex that serves as a religious, educational and cultural hub for Muslims in the Detroit area. Its modern building, opened in 2005, features a grand prayer hall, large dome and multiple community spaces, hosting major events, interfaith programs and large Friday and Ramadan congregations.
mosques.architecturalStyle: Modern Islamic with Middle Eastern influences
mosques.history: The institution was founded in 1949, with an early mosque built in 1963 to serve the growing Lebanese Shia community in Dearborn. In response to continued growth, a new 120,000-square-foot facility opened in 2005, becoming the largest mosque complex in North America and a focal point for Shia religious life and interfaith outreach.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open and welcoming to visitors; guided tours and interfaith visits are common, and modest dress is recommended.

mosques.name: Islamic Cultural Center of New York
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands weekly for prayers; significant numbers of visitors and tourists
mosques.significance: The first purpose-built mosque in New York City and a major Islamic center serving a diverse international community.
mosques.description: The Islamic Cultural Center of New York, located on Manhattan's Upper East Side, is a prominent mosque with a striking modern design, featuring a tall minaret and a cubical prayer hall capped by a dome. It serves Muslims from many countries and hosts large Friday and Eid congregations, educational programs and interfaith activities.
mosques.history: Plans for the mosque date to the 1960s, but construction took place in the 1980s with funding from several Muslim-majority countries, and the building opened in 1991 as New York's first purpose-built mosque. It quickly became a landmark institution for Muslims in the city, known for its architecture and role in interfaith dialogue.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors are welcome outside prayer times; modest dress is expected and tours may be arranged through the center.

mosques.name: Masjid Muhammad (The Nation's Mosque)
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands annually; frequent delegations and interfaith visitors
mosques.significance: Historic center of African-American Muslim life and one of the most influential mosques in the United States.
mosques.description: Masjid Muhammad in Washington, D.C., known as 'The Nation's Mosque', has played a pioneering role in the development of African-American Sunni Islam in the U.S., evolving from a Nation of Islam temple to a mainstream Sunni congregation. It is active in civic engagement, interfaith work and social justice initiatives.
mosques.history: Originating as a Nation of Islam temple, the community transitioned under Imam W. D. Mohammed in the 1970s to orthodox Sunni Islam, becoming Masjid Muhammad. It has hosted political leaders, civil-rights figures and international visitors, symbolizing the intersection of Islam and American civic life.
mosques.tourismNotes: Known for its openness to visitors and interfaith groups; contact is recommended to arrange educational visits.

mosques.name: Islamic Society of Boston Cultural Center
mosques.arabicName: المركز الثقافي للمجتمع الإسلامي في بوسطن
mosques.address: 100 Malcolm X Blvd, Roxbury, MA 02120, USA
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands annually; large Friday and Eid gatherings
mosques.significance: One of New England's largest mosques and an important cultural and educational center for Muslims in the Boston area.
mosques.description: The Islamic Society of Boston Cultural Center (ISBCC) is a large mosque and community complex in Roxbury that serves a diverse Muslim population and hosts educational, cultural and interfaith programs. Its contemporary design includes a prominent minaret and dome overlooking Malcolm X Boulevard.
mosques.history: The ISBCC project began in the 1990s, with the mosque and cultural center opening fully around 2009 as Boston's largest purpose-built mosque. It was established to provide both worship space and a broader cultural hub integrating religious education and civic engagement.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors are welcomed for tours and educational events; modest clothing is required and tours can be arranged via the center.

mosques.name: King Fahad Mosque
mosques.address: 10980 Washington Blvd, Culver City, CA 90232, USA
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands annually; major Eid and Friday congregations
mosques.significance: Architecturally prominent mosque serving a large and diverse Muslim community in the Los Angeles area.
mosques.description: The King Fahad Mosque in Culver City is known for its white marble façade, Ottoman-inspired dome and a 72-foot minaret, making it one of the most visually distinctive mosques in the United States. It serves Muslims from many ethnic backgrounds and provides religious, educational and community services.
mosques.history: Completed in the late 1990s with support from Saudi Arabia, King Fahad Mosque quickly became a central West Coast Islamic institution and a symbol of Muslim presence in Los Angeles. It frequently hosts large Eid prayers and educational programs for the broader community.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors are welcome outside prayer times; modest dress is expected and tours or visits can sometimes be arranged.

mosques.name: Dar Al-Hijrah Islamic Center
mosques.address: 3159 Row Street, Falls Church, VA 22044, USA
mosques.annualVisitors: Large weekly attendance; major regional center in the D.C. area
mosques.significance: One of the most active and influential mosques in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan region.
mosques.description: Dar Al-Hijrah Islamic Center in Falls Church is a large mosque and community center known for its extensive social services, multilingual religious programming and civic engagement. It serves a wide range of communities including Arab, African and South Asian Muslims in Northern Virginia.
mosques.history: Established in the 1980s, Dar Al-Hijrah grew from a small congregation into one of the largest mosques in the region, recognized for its role in refugee assistance, food distribution and civic participation. It has been a focal point of Muslim political and community organizing in the greater Washington area.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visits and group tours can often be arranged; the center participates in open-house programs and interfaith initiatives.

mosques.name: Islamic Center of Greater Cincinnati
mosques.address: 8092 Plantation Drive, West Chester, OH 45069, USA
mosques.significance: Major Islamic complex in the Midwest serving Muslims in the Cincinnati region and beyond.
mosques.description: The Islamic Center of Greater Cincinnati (ICGC) combines a purpose-built mosque with a full community campus that includes educational and social facilities, making it one of the most prominent Islamic institutions in the Midwest. The complex hosts worship services, classes and public outreach events.
mosques.history: ICGC opened in the mid-1990s to provide a central mosque and community center for Muslims in the Cincinnati metropolitan area. It has since grown into a regional hub for Islamic education, interfaith dialogue and cultural programming.
mosques.tourismNotes: Regular open houses and tours are offered; visitors are encouraged to dress modestly and check the center's schedule for public events.

mosques.name: East Plano Islamic Center (EPIC Masjid)
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands weekly; major North Texas congregation
mosques.significance: One of the fastest-growing and most well-known mosques in Texas, noted for its large congregation and programming.
mosques.description: The East Plano Islamic Center (EPIC Masjid) is a large suburban mosque and community center that has become widely known through its programs, scholars and strong online presence. It serves a rapidly growing Muslim population in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex.
mosques.history: EPIC began as a smaller community effort and expanded into a large purpose-built facility inaugurated around 2015 to serve the growing Muslim community in East Plano. It has since become a notable Islamic center in Texas with extensive youth and educational programs.
mosques.tourismNotes: Welcomes visitors and often appears in media and tour content about mosques in America; modest dress is requested.

mosques.name: Islamic Center of Irvine
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands weekly; large Southern California congregation
mosques.significance: Major mosque in Orange County serving a diverse and growing Muslim community.
mosques.description: The Islamic Center of Irvine (ICOI) is a large suburban mosque that serves Muslims in Irvine and surrounding areas, with extensive religious programs and youth activities. It is recognized among the largest and most active mosques in Southern California.
mosques.history: Founded in the 1990s, ICOI grew alongside the rapid expansion of Irvine and now provides prayer services, educational classes and community events for thousands of congregants. It has been highlighted in lists of major mosques in the United States.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors and schools for tours by arrangement; modest dress is expected.

mosques.name: Masjid Al-Farooq
mosques.annualVisitors: Thousands weekly; one of the main mosques in Atlanta
mosques.significance: A prominent Atlanta mosque known for its large campus, schools and community services.
mosques.description: Masjid Al-Farooq in Atlanta is recognized for its sizeable complex, including schools and a variety of services, and is a key Islamic institution in the southeastern United States. Its design features multiple domes and minarets and serves a large, diverse congregation.
mosques.history: Developed over several decades, Masjid Al-Farooq expanded from a smaller congregation into a large complex with educational institutions and burial grounds for the local Muslim community. It is frequently cited among notable mosques in North America for its size and services.
mosques.tourismNotes: Visitors can often tour the mosque and its grounds; modest clothing is required and arranging visits in advance is recommended.

mosques.name: Bishkek Central Mosque
