mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in Central Asia, funded by Turkey's Diyanet
mosques.description: Bishkek Central Mosque, also known as Imam Sarakhsi Mosque, is Kyrgyzstan's largest mosque. Built in Ottoman revival style with four minarets and marble from Turkey, it can hold 9,000 worshippers indoors and 30,000 total. Construction lasted six years and cost $25 million.
mosques.architectureNotes: Four 70-meter minarets, each with three balconies. Resembles Kocatepe Mosque in Ankara. Interior adorned with intricate tilework and chandeliers.
mosques.history: Construction began 2012, funded by Turkish Diyanet. Opened 2018. The mosque is a replica of the Kocatepe Mosque in Ankara.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. One of the largest mosques in Central Asia. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Dungan Mosque
mosques.significance: Unique wooden Chinese-style mosque built without nails by Dungan Muslim refugees
mosques.description: The Dungan Mosque was built between 1907 and 1910 by Dungan (Chinese Muslim) refugees fleeing persecution in China. Designed by a Chinese architect, it was built entirely without nails using interlocking wood. The colorful building resembles a Buddhist pagoda but serves as a mosque.
mosques.architectureNotes: Chinese pagoda-style construction. Built without nails using interlocking wood. Colors represent Dungan cultural concepts: yellow for wealth, green for happiness.
mosques.history: Built 1907–1910 by Dungan refugees who fled China in 1877. Closed by government 1933–1943. Named after Ibrahim Azhy.
mosques.tourismNotes: Popular tourist destination. The building is a unique fusion of Chinese architecture and Islamic function.

mosques.name: Imam Abu Hanifa Mosque
mosques.significance: Second largest mosque in Central Asia, named after founder of Hanafi school of Islamic jurisprudence
mosques.description: The Imam Abu Hanifa Mosque (Nu'man bin Thabit Mosque) is Tajikistan's largest mosque and one of the largest in Central Asia. Opened June 8, 2023, it can accommodate 43,000 inside and 133,000 total. The complex covers 12 hectares and includes libraries, hotels, and administrative buildings.
mosques.architectureNotes: Four minarets 75m high, main dome 47m high with 20 smaller domes. Traditional Tajik architectural patterns on walls, columns, and entrances.
mosques.history: Construction began 2009, funded by Tajik-Qatari partnership. Opened June 8, 2023 by President of Tajikistan and Emir of Qatar.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. One of the most magnificent structures in Tajikistan. Park surrounding mosque is one of the largest in Dushanbe.

mosques.name: Mosque of Islamic Solidarity
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in the Horn of Africa, national mosque of Somalia
mosques.description: The Mosque of Islamic Solidarity in Mogadishu is the largest mosque in the Horn of Africa. Completed in 1987, it overlooks the Somali Sea. Rebuilt and renovated in 2013 with Turkish funding after years of conflict damage.
mosques.history: Built 1987. Damaged during Somali Civil War. Rebuilt and renovated 2013 with Turkish assistance.
mosques.tourismNotes: Check travel advisories before visiting Somalia.

mosques.name: N'Djamena Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: Main mosque of Chad, located near Charles de Gaulle Avenue
mosques.description: The N'Djamena Grand Mosque is the main mosque in Chad's capital. Completed in 1978, it features two minarets and is centrally located near Charles de Gaulle Avenue and Avenue Félix Éboué.
mosques.history: Completed 1978. Serves as Chad's main national mosque.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in central N'Djamena. Check travel advisories.

mosques.name: Al-Naqah Mosque
mosques.significance: Oldest mosque in Tripoli, dates to Fatimid era
mosques.description: The Al-Naqah Mosque (Mosque of the Camel) is the oldest extant mosque in Tripoli, Libya. Built around 973 CE on orders of Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz, it gets its name from a legend about a camel carrying caliphal treasure. Restored in 1610.
mosques.architectureNotes: Roughly square layout, qibla wall 44m long. Fatimid-era construction with later restorations.
mosques.history: Built c. 973 CE under Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz. Oldest surviving mosque in Tripoli. Restored 1610.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in old medina. Check travel advisories for Libya.

mosques.name: Gurgi Mosque
mosques.significance: Historic Ottoman-era mosque, major tourist attraction in Tripoli's medina
mosques.description: The Gurgi Mosque is an Ottoman-era mosque in the heart of old Tripoli. Completed in 1834 by Mustafa Gurgi, it features ornate North African tiles and is located near the Roman Arch of Marcus Aurelius.
mosques.architectureNotes: Ornate tiles from North Africa. Ottoman-era decorative elements. Near Arch of Marcus Aurelius.
mosques.history: Built 1834 by Mustafa Gurgi, a naval officer. One of the best-preserved historic mosques in Tripoli.
mosques.tourismNotes: Important tourist site in Tripoli's medina. Near Arch of Marcus Aurelius and Red Castle. Check travel advisories.

mosques.name: Freetown Central Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in Sierra Leone, seat of Chief Imam
mosques.description: Freetown Central Mosque is one of the two largest mosques in Sierra Leone. Located in the capital Freetown, it serves as the seat of Sheikh Ahmad Tejan Sillah, the Chief Imam and spiritual leader of the United Council of Imams in Sierra Leone.
mosques.tourismNotes: Central location in Freetown. Seat of Sierra Leone's Chief Imam.

mosques.name: Mohammed VI Mosque
mosques.significance: Major grand mosque in Tanzania, headquarters of National Muslim Council
mosques.description: Mohammed VI Mosque is a grand mosque in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, funded by King Mohammed VI of Morocco. Completed April 15, 2022, it serves as the headquarters of the National Muslim Council of Tanzania. Built in Moorish architectural style.
mosques.architectureNotes: Moorish Revival architecture. Single minaret. Moroccan craftsmanship and design.
mosques.history: Groundbreaking October 25, 2016. Completed April 15, 2022. Funded by King Mohammed VI of Morocco.
mosques.tourismNotes: Headquarters of National Muslim Council of Tanzania. Modern facility.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Asmara
mosques.significance: One of three prominent edifices in UNESCO-listed Asmara, featuring unique minaret design
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Asmara (Al Kulafah Al Rashidan) is a mosque in central Asmara, Eritrea. Built in 1938 during Italian colonial rule, its minaret resembles a fluted Roman column. It is one of three prominent buildings in the city, alongside the Church of Our Lady of the Rosary and the Orthodox cathedral.
mosques.architectureNotes: Minaret resembles a fluted Roman column. Built during Italian colonial period. Part of Asmara's UNESCO-listed modernist architecture.
mosques.history: Built 1938 during Italian colonial rule. Designed by Guido Ferrazza. Part of Asmara's UNESCO World Heritage modernist city.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in central Asmara, a UNESCO World Heritage city. Unique colonial-era Islamic architecture.

mosques.name: Krue Se Mosque
mosques.significance: One of oldest mosques in Thailand, blend of European and Middle Eastern styles
mosques.description: Krue Se Mosque (Sultan Muzaffar Shah Mosque) is a historic mosque in Pattani Province, Thailand. Construction began in the 16th century. The surviving structure displays a mixture of Middle Eastern, European, and Pattani architectural influences. It is a designated historic site.
mosques.architectureNotes: 16th-century construction with European and Middle Eastern influences. Red brick structure. Historic landmark.
mosques.history: Construction began 16th century during Patani Sultanate. Also known as Gresik Mosque and Sultan Muzaffar Shah Mosque. Designated historic site.
mosques.tourismNotes: Historic tourist site. Located near old Patani city center. Check travel advisories for southern Thailand.

mosques.name: Husein-paša's Mosque
mosques.significance: Well-known Ottoman mosque, named after Husein-paša Boljanić
mosques.description: Husein-paša's Mosque is a historic Ottoman mosque in Pljevlja, Montenegro. Built between 1573 and 1594, it is named after Husein-paša Boljanić. It represents classic Ottoman provincial architecture and contains a museum.
mosques.architectureNotes: Classic Ottoman provincial mosque architecture. Stone construction with characteristic minaret.
mosques.history: Built 1573–1594. Named after Husein-paša Boljanić. One of the most significant Ottoman-era buildings in Montenegro.
mosques.tourismNotes: Historic monument open to visitors. Museum inside. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Badjanani Mosque
mosques.significance: Historic Friday mosque in the capital, part of Moroni's historic medina
mosques.description: The Badjanani Mosque (Ancienne Mosquée du Vendredi / Old Friday Mosque) is a historic mosque in the medina of Moroni, capital of the Comoros. Dating to the 15th–19th century, it features calligraphy, minarets, and tilework. Located near the old harbor, it is similar in style to mosques in Lamu.
mosques.architectureNotes: Traditional Comorian and Swahili coastal architecture. Calligraphy and tilework. Similar to Lamu mosques.
mosques.history: Built 15th–19th century. One of the oldest structures in Moroni. Part of the historic medina.
mosques.tourismNotes: Popular tourist spot. Located in historic medina near old harbor. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Kairouan
mosques.significance: One of oldest mosques in world, model for Maghrebi mosques, UNESCO World Heritage Site
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Kairouan (Mosque of Uqba) is one of the oldest and most important mosques in the Islamic world. Established by Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi in 670 CE, it covers over 9,000 m² and served as the model for all later mosques in the Maghreb. Part of the UNESCO World Heritage town of Kairouan.
mosques.architectureNotes: Vast quadrilateral covering 9,000 m². Courtyard 67.3m × 57.3m. Minaret 31.5m high, oldest surviving minaret in Islamic world. 414 columns in prayer hall.
mosques.history: Founded 670 CE by Uqba ibn Nafi. Current structure largely dates to 9th century Aghlabid period. Hosted University of Kairouan, a center of Islamic learning. UNESCO World Heritage since 1988.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Non-Muslims may enter courtyard but not prayer hall. In northeast of Kairouan medina.

mosques.name: Saudi Mosque
mosques.significance: Nouakchott Grand Mosque, built with Saudi assistance
mosques.description: The Saudi Mosque (Nouakchott Grand Mosque) is a major Sunni mosque in Mauritania's capital, located southwest of the Presidential Palace. Built with assistance from the Government of Saudi Arabia in 2012, it serves as a prominent landmark and center for religious activities.
mosques.architectureNotes: Modern construction with minarets. Saudi-funded. Located near Presidential Palace and Chamber of Commerce.
mosques.history: Built with Saudi Arabian government assistance. Opened 2012. Bouddah Ould Bousseyri served as imam for several decades.
mosques.tourismNotes: Major landmark in Nouakchott. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Lamido Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: Historic mosque connected to the Lamido (traditional ruler) palace in northern Cameroon
mosques.description: The Lamido Grand Mosque in Ngaoundéré is a historic mosque in northern Cameroon, closely connected to the Lamido (traditional Fulani ruler) palace. It reflects the Islamic heritage of the Adamawa region and the relationship between mosque and traditional governance.
mosques.architectureNotes: Traditional Fulani-influenced design. Connected to Lamido Palace. Stone and mud construction.
mosques.history: Built during the Fulani emirate period. Connected to the Lamido (traditional ruler) of Ngaoundéré. Center of Islamic life in Adamawa region.
mosques.tourismNotes: Part of cultural tourism in Ngaoundéré. Connected to traditional Fulani ceremonies. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Plateau Salam Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Ivory Coast's economic capital, Sudanese-style architecture
mosques.description: The Plateau Salam Mosque (Mosquée Salam du Plateau) is a major mosque in Abidjan's Plateau district. Inaugurated in 2007 after construction began in 1996, it features a vivid blue dome with gold design and a 65-meter minaret. Inspired by Silk Route Central Asian architecture, it accommodates 6,500 worshippers.
mosques.architectureNotes: Vivid blue dome with gold design. 65-meter minaret. Four floors: parking, ablution areas, main prayer hall, women's section. Silk Route-inspired.
mosques.history: First stone laid 1994 by President Henri Konan Bédié. Construction began 1996. Inaugurated 2007. Financial assistance from Middle East.
mosques.tourismNotes: Popular tourist attraction. Located in Plateau district downtown. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Surti Sunni Jamah Mosque
mosques.significance: Oldest surviving Muslim place of worship in Yangon, built during British colonial era
mosques.description: The Surti Sunni Jamah Mosque is believed to be Yangon's oldest surviving Muslim place of worship. Built in the 1860s on what was then Mughal Street, it features imposing twin minarets and a large arched entrance. The mosque serves the Indian Muslim community that arrived during British colonial rule.
mosques.architectureNotes: Twin minarets. Large arched entrance tower. Built during British colonial period. On former Mughal Street.
mosques.history: Built ca. 1860s on Mughal (Shwebontha) Street, heart of 'Indian' Yangon. Served courtiers and attendants of exiled Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar who was exiled to Rangoon in 1857.
mosques.tourismNotes: Historic site in downtown Yangon. Part of colonial-era walking tours. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Maputo Central Mosque
mosques.significance: Main mosque in Mozambique's capital, center of Islamic community activities
mosques.description: The Maputo Central Mosque (Grand Mosque) is the main mosque in Mozambique's capital, inaugurated in early 2003. Built by the Islamic community after obtaining permission for construction in downtown Maputo, it serves as a center for religious services and community activities.
mosques.architectureNotes: Modern construction. White facade with green accents. Minaret. Downtown Maputo location.
mosques.history: Completed and inaugurated early 2003. Built after government granted permission for new mosques in city centers. Islamic community construction project.
mosques.tourismNotes: Center of Islamic community in Maputo. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Quba Mosque
mosques.significance: First mosque built in Islam, constructed by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
mosques.description: Quba Mosque is the oldest mosque in the world. Prophet Muhammad ﷺ laid its foundation stones upon arriving in Medina during the Hijrah in 622 CE. The Prophet said that praying two rak'ahs in Quba Mosque is equivalent to performing Umrah. It has been expanded multiple times throughout history.
mosques.architectureNotes: Modern expansions preserve the sacred site. Multiple domes, minarets, and large courtyards. White marble finish.
mosques.history: Founded 622 CE by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ during the Hijrah. First mosque in Islam. Original structure simple mud-brick. Expanded by Umayyads, Abbasids, Ottomans, and Saudi government. Current structure from 1986 expansion.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims may not enter. Part of the Ziyarah (visit) for pilgrims in Medina. Best visited on Saturday (Sunnah tradition).

mosques.name: Mosque of Amr ibn al-As
mosques.significance: First mosque in Africa and Egypt, built by the conqueror of Egypt
mosques.description: The Mosque of Amr ibn al-As is the oldest mosque in Egypt and Africa. Built in 642 CE by the Arab commander Amr ibn al-As after conquering Egypt, it was originally a simple structure that has been rebuilt and expanded many times. Known as the 'Crown of Mosques' and 'Taj al-Jawami'.
mosques.architectureNotes: Original mosque was simple mud-brick. Current structure dates from various reconstructions. Rectangular hypostyle plan. Over 200 columns.
mosques.history: Built 642 CE by Amr ibn al-As after conquest of Egypt. Originally 29m × 17m. Rebuilt multiple times: Umayyad (698), Abbasid (827), Fatimid, and later periods. Current structure largely 1875 reconstruction.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in Old Cairo (Fustat). Open to visitors outside prayer times. Modest dress required. Near Coptic Cairo and other historic sites.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Kufa
mosques.significance: One of earliest mosques in Islam, important Shia pilgrimage site, fourth holiest site in Shia Islam
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Kufa (Masjid al-Kufa) is one of the oldest mosques in the world. Built in 639 CE during the Rashidun Caliphate, it is the fourth holiest site in Shia Islam. The mosque contains the mihrab where Imam Ali was martyred in 661 CE. It is built on land purchased from an Arab Christian.
mosques.architectureNotes: Large rectangular plan. Contains several shrines including those attributed to Prophet Nuh (Noah), Muslim ibn Aqil, and the maqam of Imam Ali.
mosques.history: Founded 639 CE during caliphate of Umar. Site where Imam Ali established his capital (656-661). Location of Ali's assassination (661). Major pilgrimage site for Shia Muslims. Rebuilt multiple times.
mosques.tourismNotes: Major Shia pilgrimage destination. Near Imam Ali Shrine in Najaf. Modest dress required. Women need to wear chador.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Basra
mosques.significance: One of earliest mosques, center of early Islamic scholarship
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Basra was one of the first mosques built outside Arabia. Founded in 647 CE during the caliphate of Umar, it became a major center of Islamic learning and scholarship. Famous scholars like Hasan al-Basri taught here. The original mosque has been rebuilt multiple times.
mosques.architectureNotes: Current structure is modern reconstruction. Original was simple hypostyle mosque. Site of early Islamic scholarly activity.
mosques.history: Founded 647 CE by Utbah ibn Ghazwan. Basra was second city founded in Islam (after Kufa). Center of Arabic grammar development. Home of Hasan al-Basri (642-728). Rebuilt multiple times due to wars and damage.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in Basra city center. Historic significance for Islamic scholarship. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Córdoba
mosques.significance: Pinnacle of Moorish architecture in Al-Andalus, UNESCO World Heritage Site
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Córdoba (Mezquita) is one of the greatest works of Islamic architecture. Built by Abd al-Rahman I in 785 CE, it was expanded over centuries to become the second-largest mosque in the world. After the Reconquista (1236), it was converted to a cathedral. The forest of 856 columns and double arches remains one of architecture's greatest achievements.
mosques.architectureNotes: Famous horseshoe arches with red and white voussoirs. 856 columns of jasper, onyx, marble, and granite. Hypostyle hall covering 23,400 m². Mihrab decorated with Byzantine mosaics. Original minaret converted to bell tower.
mosques.history: Built 785 CE by Abd al-Rahman I on site of Visigothic church. Expanded by Abd al-Rahman II (833), Al-Hakam II (961), and Al-Mansur (987). Converted to cathedral 1236 after Reconquista. UNESCO World Heritage since 1984.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Now Córdoba Cathedral-Mosque (Mezquita-Catedral). Open to visitors. Entry fee applies. Prayer by Muslims not currently permitted.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Samarra
mosques.significance: Once largest mosque in the world, iconic spiral Malwiya minaret, UNESCO World Heritage Site
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Samarra was once the largest mosque in the world. Built during the Abbasid Caliphate (848-851 CE), it is famous for its massive spiral minaret (Malwiya), standing 52 meters tall. The mosque covered 42 acres and could hold over 100,000 worshippers. Now largely in ruins, it remains an iconic symbol of Islamic architecture.
mosques.architectureNotes: Massive rectangular enclosure 240m × 156m. Famous Malwiya (spiral) minaret 52m high with external spiral ramp. Outer walls have 44 semicircular towers. Inspired by Mesopotamian ziggurats.
mosques.history: Built 848-851 CE by Abbasid Caliph al-Mutawakkil. Largest mosque of its time. Part of Samarra capital complex. Damaged by Mongol invasion (1258). Now in ruins. UNESCO World Heritage since 2007.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Archaeological site with ruins. Malwiya minaret is climbable. Located in Samarra, north of Baghdad. Security situation may affect access.

mosques.name: Grand Mosalla of Tehran
mosques.significance: Planned to become world's largest mosque complex
mosques.description: The Grand Mosalla of Tehran (Imam Khomeini Mosalla) is a massive under-construction mosque and prayer complex intended as the central venue for Tehran's Friday prayers and religious events. Initiated in the 1980s, it is undergoing expansion to 200 hectares and is planned to become the world's largest mosque complex.
mosques.architectureNotes: Under construction since 1989. Designed by Mohammad-Reza Haeri Mazandarani. Will include massive dome, minarets, and cultural facilities.
mosques.history: Construction began 1989. Designed to replace multiple city prayer spaces. Hosts Tehran International Book Fair. Ongoing expansion planned to make it world's largest mosque complex.
mosques.tourismNotes: Partially open for events and prayers. Hosts Tehran International Book Fair annually. Construction ongoing.

mosques.name: Nusantara National Mosque
mosques.significance: Future state mosque of Indonesia's new capital
mosques.description: The Nusantara National Mosque is being built in Indonesia's new capital city (IKN) to replace Istiqlal Mosque in Jakarta as the state mosque. Groundbreaking ceremony was held in January 2024 by President Joko Widodo. It will serve as a symbol of national unity and religious harmony.
mosques.architectureNotes: Design inspired by Indonesian cultural elements. Will feature modern Islamic architecture with local influences.
mosques.history: Groundbreaking January 2024 by President Jokowi. Part of new capital city development. Designed to symbolize national unity.
mosques.tourismNotes: Under construction. Part of new capital development.

mosques.name: Djamaa el Djazaïr
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Africa, third-largest in the world, tallest minaret in the world
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Algiers (Djamaa el Djazaïr) is the largest mosque in Africa and third-largest in the world after Mecca and Medina. Its minaret at 265m (870 ft) is the world's tallest. Inaugurated in 2019, the complex includes a Quran school for 300 students, a library holding one million books, and a museum of Islamic art.
mosques.architectureNotes: World's tallest minaret at 265m. Central dome 50m diameter. Seismic-resistant to 9.0 Richter. Retractable roof. Chinese-built.
mosques.history: Construction 2012-2019 by CSCEC (China). Cost $1.5 billion. Inaugurated April 2019 for Ramadan. Designed by German firm KSP Jürgen Engel Architekten.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Guided tours available. Largest mosque in Africa. Near Mediterranean coast.

mosques.name: King Fahd Islamic Cultural Center
mosques.address: Av. Int. Bullrich 55, Palermo, Buenos Aires
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Latin America
mosques.description: The King Fahd Islamic Cultural Center is the largest mosque in Latin America. Inaugurated in 2000, it was funded by Saudi Arabia on land granted by President Carlos Menem. The complex features a large prayer hall for 1,500 men and 500 women, a library, and educational facilities.
mosques.architectureNotes: Ottoman-inspired design. 34,000 m² complex. Large dome and minaret. Landscaped gardens.
mosques.history: Construction 1995-2000. Funded by King Fahd of Saudi Arabia. Land granted in 1995 by President Carlos Menem. Named after the king.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free guided tours available monthly. Open to non-Muslims. Located in Palermo neighborhood.

mosques.name: Lakemba Mosque
mosques.significance: Sydney's oldest purpose-built mosque, Australia's largest
mosques.description: Lakemba Mosque (Ali Ibn Abi Talib Mosque) is Sydney's oldest purpose-built mosque and one of Australia's largest. Completed in 1977, it serves as a major center for the Muslim community, especially during Ramadan when thousands gather for Eid prayers.
mosques.architectureNotes: Purpose-built design. Large prayer hall. Minaret. Community facilities.
mosques.history: Built 1977 by Lebanese Muslim Association. Expanded multiple times. Australia's most prominent mosque during Ramadan.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Famous for Ramadan night markets. Located in Sydney's southwest.

mosques.name: Melbourne Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Victoria, Australia's first grand mosque
mosques.description: The Melbourne Grand Mosque opened in 2022 after a decade of planning. Located in Tarneit in Melbourne's west, it is Victoria's largest mosque and Australia's first 'grand mosque.' It serves as a community hub promoting harmony and interfaith dialogue.
mosques.architectureNotes: Contemporary grand mosque design. Large dome and minarets. Community facilities.
mosques.history: Decade-long project. Funded by Werribee Islamic Centre and community donations. Opened March 2022.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to all faiths. Located in Melbourne's western growth corridor.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Paris
mosques.address: 2bis Place du Puits de l'Ermite, 75005 Paris
mosques.significance: Oldest and largest mosque in France, cultural landmark
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Paris is the oldest and largest mosque in France. Built in 1926 in Hispano-Moorish style, it was created to honor Muslim soldiers who fought for France in World War I. The complex includes a prayer hall, courtyard, garden, restaurant, and hammam.
mosques.architectureNotes: 33m minaret. Moroccan-inspired architecture with zellige tiles, carved stucco. Courtyard with fountain. Prayer hall with marble columns.
mosques.history: Built 1922-1926 to honor Muslim soldiers in WWI. Dedicated by French President Gaston Doumergue and Sultan Moulay Youssef of Morocco.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors outside prayer times. Famous restaurant and salon de thé. Hammam open to public. Near Jardin des Plantes.

mosques.name: Mosque of Rome
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in the Western world
mosques.description: The Mosque of Rome is the largest mosque in the Western world. Designed by Paolo Portoghesi and inaugurated in 1995, it serves as the seat of the Islamic Cultural Centre of Italy. The design blends Islamic and Italian architectural traditions.
mosques.architectureNotes: Designed by Paolo Portoghesi. Forest-like interior with tree-shaped columns. 30,000 m² complex. Blends Islamic and Italian elements.
mosques.history: Construction 1984-1995. Funded by Saudi Arabia and Muslim countries. Land donated by Rome municipality. Designed by Paolo Portoghesi.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Located in Parioli area near Villa Ada park.

mosques.name: London Central Mosque
mosques.significance: One of UK's largest and most prominent mosques
mosques.description: London Central Mosque, also known as Regent's Park Mosque, is one of the UK's most prominent mosques. Designed by Sir Frederick Gibberd with its distinctive golden dome, it opened in 1977 and serves as a major Islamic center for London's Muslim community.
mosques.architectureNotes: Golden dome landmark. Designed by Sir Frederick Gibberd. Main hall holds 5,000. Women's gallery.
mosques.history: Established 1940 with government land grant. Building completed 1977 after international design competition won by Frederick Gibberd.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Near Regent's Park. Educational tours available.

mosques.name: East London Mosque
mosques.significance: One of UK's largest mosques, London's oldest mosque trust
mosques.description: The East London Mosque is one of the largest mosques in the UK. The mosque trust dates to 1910, making it London's oldest. The current building opened in 1985, with the adjacent London Muslim Centre added in 2004. It serves the diverse Muslim community of Tower Hamlets.
mosques.architectureNotes: Brick construction. Minaret. Expanded with London Muslim Centre (2004) and Maryam Centre (2013) for women.
mosques.history: Trust established 1910. Current mosque building 1985. London Muslim Centre 2004. Maryam Centre 2013.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Located in Whitechapel. Educational programs available.

mosques.name: Cologne Central Mosque
mosques.significance: One of Europe's largest mosques, modern architectural landmark
mosques.description: The Cologne Central Mosque (DITIB-Zentralmoschee) is one of the largest mosques in Europe. Designed by Paul Böhm, it features a distinctive modern design with a transparent glass facade. Officially inaugurated by President Erdoğan in 2018, it cost €50 million to build.
mosques.architectureNotes: Designed by Paul Böhm. Striking modern design with 55m dome, glass facade. Two 55m minarets. €50 million cost.
mosques.history: Groundbreaking 2009. Opened for prayer 2017. Official inauguration 2018 by Turkish President Erdoğan. Operated by DITIB.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Guided tours available. Located in Ehrenfeld district.

mosques.name: Cambridge Central Mosque
mosques.significance: UK's first eco-mosque, award-winning sustainable design
mosques.description: Cambridge Central Mosque is Europe's first purpose-built eco-mosque. Designed by Marks Barfield Architects, it opened in 2019. The timber interior evokes a 'grove of trees' and features sustainable design including natural ventilation, rainwater harvesting, and heat pumps.
mosques.architectureNotes: Timber 'grove of trees' interior. Skylights. Natural ventilation. Rainwater harvesting. Heat pumps. Designed by Marks Barfield.
mosques.history: Decade in planning. Cost £23 million. Opened April 2019. Officially opened December 2019 by President Erdoğan and Yusuf Islam (Cat Stevens).
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Award-winning architecture. Located on Mill Road.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Xi'an
mosques.address: 30 Huajue Lane, Lianhu District, Xi'an, Shaanxi
mosques.significance: One of China's oldest and largest mosques, blending Chinese and Islamic architecture
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Xi'an is one of the oldest and most renowned mosques in China, founded in 742 during the Tang Dynasty. Unlike most mosques, it follows traditional Chinese temple architecture with courtyards, gardens, and pavilions, while maintaining Islamic elements. No minarets—instead, a traditional Chinese pagoda-style structure serves as the minaret.
mosques.architectureNotes: Tang Dynasty foundation (742). Chinese courtyard layout with Islamic orientation. No traditional dome or minaret. Wooden structures and Chinese calligraphy. UNESCO tentative list.
mosques.history: Founded 742 CE during Tang Dynasty. Expanded during Ming (1392) and Qing dynasties. One of four great mosques of China. Serves Xi'an's Hui Muslim community.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to tourists. Located in Muslim Quarter. Active mosque—respectful dress required. Small entrance fee.

mosques.name: Niujie Mosque
mosques.significance: Oldest and largest mosque in Beijing
mosques.description: Niujie Mosque (Ox Street Mosque) is the oldest and largest mosque in Beijing, founded in 996 CE during the Liao Dynasty. Rebuilt in the Ming Dynasty (1442), it exemplifies Chinese-Islamic architecture with traditional Chinese rooflines and Islamic interior decoration.
mosques.architectureNotes: Liao Dynasty foundation (996). Ming Dynasty rebuilding (1442). Chinese temple-style exterior. 42m minaret (Wangyue Lou). Prayer hall with Arabic calligraphy.
mosques.history: Founded 996 CE by Arab cleric Nasruddin. Rebuilt 1442 during Ming Dynasty. Expanded under Qing emperors Kangxi and Qianlong. Major renovation 1996.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors outside prayer times. Located in Beijing's Muslim Quarter. Respectful dress required.

mosques.name: Tokyo Camii & Turkish Cultural Center
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Japan
mosques.description: Tokyo Camii is the largest mosque in Japan, located in Shibuya. The original mosque was built by Tatar refugees in 1938 and rebuilt in 2000 in Ottoman architectural style. The Turkish Cultural Center below promotes interfaith dialogue. It's one of Asia's most beautiful mosques.
mosques.architectureNotes: Ottoman-style architecture with 23m dome. Two minarets. Interior tiles from Turkey. Rebuilt 2000 with Turkish government support.
mosques.history: Original mosque 1938 by Tatar Muslim refugees. Demolished 1986 due to decay. Rebuilt 2000 funded by Turkish government. Opened June 30, 2000.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to all visitors. Free guided tours. Near Yoyogi-Uehara Station. No photography during prayers.

mosques.name: Seoul Central Mosque
mosques.significance: First purpose-built mosque in South Korea
mosques.description: Seoul Central Mosque was the first purpose-built mosque in South Korea, opened in 1976 with funding from Muslim countries. Located in the Itaewon district, it serves as the headquarters of the Korea Muslim Federation and the spiritual center for Korea's Muslim community.
mosques.architectureNotes: Distinctive Ottoman-influenced design. Two minarets. Dome. Located on hillside in Itaewon.
mosques.history: Opened May 21, 1976. Funded by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, UAE, and other Muslim countries. Korea Muslim Federation headquarters.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Located in Itaewon. Many halal restaurants nearby. Respectful dress required.

mosques.name: Brazil Mosque (Mesquita Brasil)
mosques.address: Rua Barão de Jaguara, 1162, Cambuci, São Paulo
mosques.significance: Oldest mosque in South America
mosques.description: Mesquita Brasil (Brazil Mosque), originally called São Paulo Mosque, is considered the oldest mosque in South America, founded in 1929. Built by Syrian and Lebanese immigrants, it was renamed 'Brazil Mosque' to avoid the Christian saint's name. A historic landmark of Muslim presence in Latin America.
mosques.architectureNotes: 1929 construction. Moorish-influenced architecture with arches. Modest size. Historic community center.
mosques.history: Founded 1929 by Syrian-Lebanese immigrants. Originally 'São Paulo Mosque', renamed 'Brazil Mosque' in 1969. One of Brazil's first mosques.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Located in Cambuci neighborhood. Historic significance.

mosques.name: Omar Ibn Al-Khattab Mosque
mosques.address: Av. Juscelino Kubitschek, Foz do Iguaçu, Paraná
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Latin America, tourist landmark near Iguazu Falls
mosques.description: The Omar Ibn Al-Khattab Mosque in Foz do Iguaçu is one of the largest mosques in Latin America. Located in the tri-border region (Brazil-Argentina-Paraguay), it serves the local Arab community and is a tourist attraction near the famous Iguazu Falls. Its distinctive minaret is a city landmark.
mosques.architectureNotes: Prominent minaret. Modern construction. Located in tri-border area with significant Arab population.
mosques.history: Inaugurated 1983. Serves large Arab immigrant community in Foz do Iguaçu. Tourist landmark near Iguazu Falls.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Near Iguazu Falls. Part of tri-border tourism circuit.

mosques.name: Auburn Gallipoli Mosque
mosques.significance: Major Ottoman-style mosque in Sydney, landmark for Turkish-Australian community
mosques.description: Auburn Gallipoli Mosque is one of Sydney's most prominent mosques, serving the Turkish-Australian community. Built in Ottoman style with distinctive domes and minarets, it commemorates the Gallipoli campaign and serves as a center for the Auburn Muslim community.
mosques.architectureNotes: Ottoman-style with dome and two minarets. Named after Gallipoli (Gelibolu). Landmark beside Main Western Railway.
mosques.history: Foundation stone 1986. Completed 1999. Named to commemorate Gallipoli campaign and Turkish-Australian heritage.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Located near Auburn station. Part of Auburn's multicultural precinct.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Brussels
mosques.significance: Oldest and largest mosque in Belgium, housed in historic Oriental Pavilion
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Brussels, also known as the Islamic Cultural Centre of Belgium, is housed in the Oriental Pavilion in Cinquantenaire Park. The building was constructed in 1880 for a world exhibition and converted to a mosque in 1978. It serves as Belgium's primary Islamic center.
mosques.architectureNotes: Originally 1880 Oriental Pavilion. Neo-Moorish architecture. Converted 1978 with Saudi funding. Part of Cinquantenaire Park.
mosques.history: Building erected 1880 for National Exhibition. Donated by King Baudouin 1967. Converted to mosque 1978 with Saudi Arabian support.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in Cinquantenaire Park. Historic architecture. Check visiting hours.

mosques.name: Essalam Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in the Netherlands, one of the largest in Europe
mosques.description: Essalam Mosque is the largest mosque in the Netherlands and often cited as one of the largest in Europe. Funded by the Al Maktoum Foundation (UAE), it opened in 2010 after years of controversy. Its distinctive domes and minarets make it a Rotterdam landmark.
mosques.architectureNotes: 50m minarets (among tallest in Europe). Large central dome. Capacity 3,000. Funded by UAE.
mosques.history: Years of planning and controversy. Funded by Al Maktoum Foundation (Dubai). Opened December 2010.
mosques.tourismNotes: Rotterdam landmark. Open to visitors at designated times.

mosques.name: Mevlana Mosque
mosques.significance: Major Turkish mosque in Netherlands, Ottoman-style architecture
mosques.description: Mevlana Mosque is one of the largest Turkish mosques in the Netherlands. Named after Mevlana Jalaluddin Rumi, it features Ottoman-inspired architecture with a prominent dome and minaret. It serves Rotterdam's Turkish Muslim community.
mosques.architectureNotes: Ottoman-style with dome and minaret. Named after Mevlana Rumi. Opened 2001.
mosques.history: Opened 2001. Serves Turkish community. Named after Sufi mystic Mevlana Jalaluddin Rumi.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Part of Rotterdam's multicultural landscape.

mosques.name: Suraya Mosque (Dar As-Salam)
mosques.significance: First purpose-built mosque in Mexico
mosques.description: Suraya Mosque, also known as Dar As-Salam, is considered the first purpose-built mosque in Mexico. Located in Torreón, it serves the local Muslim community, which traces its roots to Lebanese immigrants. It marks an important milestone in Mexican Islamic history.
mosques.architectureNotes: First mosque in Mexico. Modest but historically significant.
mosques.history: Established by Lebanese-Mexican Muslim community. First purpose-built mosque in Mexico.
mosques.tourismNotes: Historic significance. Check visiting hours.

mosques.name: Ban Ho Mosque
mosques.significance: Main mosque of Chiang Mai's Hui Muslim community
mosques.description: Ban Ho Mosque (Masjid Hedayatul Islam) is the main mosque of Chiang Mai's Hui Muslim community, descendants of Chinese Muslim traders who settled in northern Thailand. Built in 1917, it blends Thai and Chinese architectural elements with Islamic design.
mosques.architectureNotes: Blend of Thai, Chinese, and Islamic styles. Serves Hui Muslim community (Chin Haw). Two buildings: prayer hall and educational hall.
mosques.history: Built 1917 by Yunnan Chinese Muslims (Hui/Chin Haw). Community descended from caravan traders on ancient trade routes.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Located in Chiang Mai's Muslim quarter near Chang Moi Road.

mosques.name: Al Noor Mosque
mosques.address: 12 Hang Luoc Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi
mosques.significance: Only mosque in Northern Vietnam, over 130 years old
mosques.description: Al Noor Mosque is the only mosque in northern Vietnam, built in 1890 by Indian merchants. Located in Hanoi's Old Quarter, it has served the Muslim community for over 130 years. The mosque features Indo-Islamic architecture painted in green and white.
mosques.architectureNotes: Built by Indian subcontinent community. Green and white exterior. Small but historically significant.
mosques.history: Built 1890 by Indian Muslim merchants. Survived multiple periods of conflict. Remains active with five daily prayers.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in Hanoi Old Quarter (36 streets). Visitors welcome. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Masjid Al-Dahab (Manila Golden Mosque)
mosques.address: Globo de Oro Street, Quiapo, Manila
mosques.significance: Landmark mosque in Manila, symbol of Filipino Muslim heritage
mosques.description: The Manila Golden Mosque (Masjid Al-Dahab) is a stunning mosque in Quiapo, Manila, built in 1976. Its golden dome makes it one of the most recognizable landmarks in Manila's Muslim district. It serves as a cultural and religious hub for the Filipino Muslim community.
mosques.architectureNotes: Striking golden dome. Built 1976 during Marcos era. Cultural center for Filipino Muslims.
mosques.history: Built 1976 under Ferdinand Marcos administration with Libyan funding. Named Al-Dahab (Golden) for its distinctive golden dome.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in Quiapo Muslim district. Open to visitors. Photography allowed outside.

mosques.name: Stockholm Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Stockholm, converted Art Nouveau power station
mosques.description: Stockholm Mosque is the largest Muslim prayer space in Stockholm. Originally built as an electric power station in 1903 by Art Nouveau architect Ferdinand Boberg, the building was converted to a mosque in the 1990s. Its Moorish-influenced original design made it suitable for conversion.
mosques.architectureNotes: Originally 1903 power station by Ferdinand Boberg. Moorish-influenced Art Nouveau. Converted to mosque 1990s. Capacity 2,000.
mosques.history: Building completed 1903 as electric power station. Moorish design by Ferdinand Boberg. Converted to mosque during 1990s.
mosques.tourismNotes: Central Stockholm location. Part of Aga Khan Trust architectural heritage.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Copenhagen
mosques.significance: First purpose-built non-Ahmadiyya mosque in Denmark, one of largest in Europe
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque of Copenhagen, officially the Hamad Bin Khalifa Civilisation Center, opened in 2014. It is the first purpose-built mainstream mosque in Denmark and one of the largest mosques in Northern Europe, covering 6,700 square meters.
mosques.architectureNotes: 6,700 m² complex. Modern design with dome. First purpose-built mosque in Denmark. Named after Qatari Emir.
mosques.history: Opened June 2014. Funded by Qatar. Named Hamad Bin Khalifa Civilisation Center after Qatari Emir. First non-Ahmadiyya purpose-built mosque in Denmark.
mosques.tourismNotes: Located in Nørrebro neighborhood. Guided tours available. Open to visitors.

mosques.name: Geneva Mosque
mosques.significance: One of Switzerland's largest mosques, has one of four minarets in country
mosques.description: The Geneva Mosque is one of the largest mosques in Switzerland, opened in 1978 with funding from Saudi Arabia. It features one of only four minarets in Switzerland (construction of new minarets was banned by referendum in 2009).
mosques.architectureNotes: One of four minarets in Switzerland. Saudi-funded. Simple modern design.
mosques.history: Opened 1978. Funded by Saudi Arabia. One of few mosques with minaret in Switzerland (minaret ban 2009).
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Check visiting hours.

mosques.name: Mahmood Mosque
mosques.significance: First purpose-built mosque in Switzerland
mosques.description: The Mahmood Mosque in Zurich is the first purpose-built mosque in Switzerland, opened in 1963. It is owned by the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community and features a minaret, the construction of which is now banned in Switzerland.
mosques.architectureNotes: First mosque in Switzerland. Has minaret (now banned for new construction). Ahmadiyya community.
mosques.history: Foundation stone laid 1962 by daughter of Mirza Ghulam Ahmad. Inaugurated 1963 by Sir Muhammad Zafrulla Khan. First purpose-built mosque in Switzerland.
mosques.tourismNotes: Historic significance. Open to visitors.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Granada
mosques.significance: First mosque in Granada since 1492 Reconquista, overlooks the Alhambra
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Granada, opened in 2003, is the first mosque built in Granada since the Christian Reconquista of 1492. Located in the historic Albaicín neighborhood with views of the Alhambra, it features traditional Nasrid-style architecture.
mosques.architectureNotes: Nasrid Empire style. Gardens with Alhambra views. First mosque in Granada since 1492. Plaza San Nicolás location.
mosques.history: Opened July 2003. First mosque in Granada since 1492 Reconquista. Funded by UAE and other Muslim countries. 500-year restoration of Muslim presence.
mosques.tourismNotes: Spectacular Alhambra views. Garden open to visitors. Tea house. Located in Albaicín UNESCO World Heritage area.

mosques.name: Koutoubia Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Marrakesh, iconic 77-meter minaret inspired Giralda in Seville
mosques.description: The Koutoubia Mosque is the largest mosque in Marrakesh, Morocco. Built by the Almohad Caliph Abd al-Mu'min between 1147 and 1158, its 77-meter minaret is an iconic Marrakesh landmark and inspired the Giralda in Seville and Hassan Tower in Rabat.
mosques.architectureNotes: 77-meter minaret (lantern adds 12m). Red stone construction. T-plan layout from Kairouan tradition. Four gilded copper globes crown the minaret.
mosques.history: Built 1147-1158 by Almohad Caliph Abd al-Mu'min. Actually two mosques built at same site. Name means 'Mosque of the Booksellers' from nearby souk.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims cannot enter interior. Minaret visible throughout Marrakesh. Beautiful illumination at night. Near Jemaa el-Fnaa square.

mosques.name: Al-Qarawiyyin Mosque
mosques.significance: World's oldest continually operating university, founded 859 CE
mosques.description: Al-Qarawiyyin Mosque and University is recognized by UNESCO and Guinness World Records as the oldest continually operating university in the world. Founded in 859 CE by Fatima al-Fihri, it has been a leading center of Islamic scholarship for over 1,100 years.
mosques.architectureNotes: Multiple courtyards. Historic library. One of the world's oldest educational institutions. Intricate zellige tilework, carved plaster, and cedar wood.
mosques.history: Founded 859 CE by Fatima al-Fihri. World's oldest continually operating university per UNESCO. Expanded through Almoravid, Almohad, and Marinid periods.
mosques.tourismNotes: Non-Muslims cannot enter prayer hall. Courtyard partially visible. Nearby Al-Attarine Madrasa open to visitors.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Aleppo
mosques.significance: One of the oldest mosques in the world, severely damaged in Syrian Civil War
mosques.description: The Great Umayyad Mosque of Aleppo was one of the largest and oldest mosques in Syria, founded in the 8th century. Its 45-meter minaret (built 1090) was destroyed in 2013 during the Syrian Civil War. Reconstruction began in 2025.
mosques.architectureNotes: Founded 8th century. 45-meter Seljuk minaret (1090) destroyed 2013. Contains shrine of Zechariah (father of John the Baptist). Hellenistic agora site.
mosques.history: Site was Hellenistic agora, then Byzantine cathedral. Mosque built under Umayyads (715). Minaret added 1090. Severely damaged 2012-2016. Reconstruction started 2025.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO World Heritage as part of Ancient City of Aleppo. Currently under reconstruction. Check access before visiting.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Sana'a
mosques.significance: One of the oldest mosques in the world, allegedly built during Prophet's lifetime
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Sana'a is one of the oldest mosques in the world, said to have been founded by the Prophet Muhammad himself in 633 CE. It contains ancient Quran manuscripts discovered in 1972. Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Old City of Sana'a.
mosques.architectureNotes: One of the world's oldest mosques. Ancient Quranic manuscripts found 1972 (Sana'a manuscripts). Pre-Islamic spolia incorporated.
mosques.history: Allegedly founded 633 CE by companion of Prophet Muhammad. Renovated under Caliph al-Walid I (705-715). Multiple restorations. Important Sana'a manuscripts discovered 1972.
mosques.tourismNotes: Part of UNESCO Old City of Sana'a. Check current travel advisories for Yemen.

mosques.name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Lebanon, burial site of PM Rafik Hariri
mosques.description: The Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque (Blue Mosque) is Beirut's largest mosque, built by Prime Minister Rafik Hariri and opened in 2008. Its distinctive blue domes and 72-meter minarets dominate the Beirut skyline. Hariri is buried beside the mosque.
mosques.architectureNotes: Blue domes inspired by Sultan Ahmed Mosque. Ottoman style with Mamluk touches. Four 72-meter minarets. 10,000 m² complex.
mosques.history: Built 2002-2007 by PM Rafik Hariri. Inaugurated October 2008 by PM Saad Hariri. Hariri buried beside mosque after 2005 assassination.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Central Beirut location near Martyrs' Square. Photography permitted outside.

mosques.name: Grand Mosque of Kuwait
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Kuwait, national mosque
mosques.description: The Grand Mosque is the largest and most prominent mosque in Kuwait. Covering 45,000 m² with a 20,000 m² building, it features a 26-meter diameter dome and a 74-meter minaret. Built at a cost of 13 million Kuwaiti Dinars (~$48 million).
mosques.architectureNotes: 45,000 m² site. 26m dome, 43m high. 74m Andalusian-style minaret. Cost 13M KWD (~$48M).
mosques.history: Completed 1986. Kuwait's national mosque. Faced Al-Seif Palace on Arabian Gulf Street.
mosques.tourismNotes: Tours available for non-Muslims. Modest dress required. Opposite Al-Seif Palace.

mosques.name: Al-Fateh Grand Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in the world, houses Bahrain's National Library
mosques.description: Al-Fateh Grand Mosque is one of the largest mosques in the world, accommodating over 7,000 worshippers. Named after Ahmed Al Fateh, founder of Bahrain. Since 2006, it houses the National Library of Bahrain. Its massive fibreglass dome weighs over 60 tonnes.
mosques.architectureNotes: 6,500 m² footprint. Fibreglass dome (60+ tonnes). Italian marble, Austrian glass, teak from India. National Library since 2006.
mosques.history: Built 1987 by Sheikh Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa. Named after Ahmed Al Fateh (Bahrain founder). National Library added 2006.
mosques.tourismNotes: Free tours for non-Muslims. Modest dress required. Library open to public.

mosques.name: Al-Aqmar Mosque
mosques.significance: Seminal Fatimid architecture, first mosque aligned to street grid
mosques.description: Al-Aqmar Mosque is a Fatimid-era mosque built in 1125, famous for its ornate carved stone facade—the earliest of its kind in Cairo. Its alignment to the street grid while maintaining qibla orientation influenced later Cairo mosque design.
mosques.architectureNotes: First Cairo mosque with decorated stone facade. Aligned to street grid. Ismaili Shia symbolism. Cylindrical finial from Ottoman era.
mosques.history: Built 1125 by Fatimid vizier al-Ma'mun al-Bata'ihi. Important monument in Cairo's architectural evolution. Restored multiple times.
mosques.tourismNotes: Part of Historic Cairo walking route. On Al-Muizz Street. Open to visitors.

mosques.name: Nur-Astana Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in Central Asia, landmark of Astana
mosques.description: Nur-Astana Mosque was Kazakhstan's main Friday mosque before the Astana Grand Mosque opened. Completed in 2005, it features a 40m dome and four 63m minarets, blending modern design with Islamic architectural traditions.
mosques.architectureNotes: 40m central dome, four 63m minarets. White granite and marble exterior. Capacity doubled original plans.
mosques.history: Built 2005 with funding from Qatar. Named 'Light of Astana'. Was the primary mosque until Hazrat Sultan Mosque opened in 2012.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Modest dress required. Located in central Astana near the river.

mosques.name: Central Mosque of Almaty
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Almaty, Kazakhstan's main commercial city
mosques.description: The Central Mosque of Almaty is the main congregational mosque of Kazakhstan's largest city. Its blue domes and white minarets are visible across the city, serving as a major religious and community center.
mosques.architectureNotes: Large blue dome, multiple smaller domes. White marble exterior. Traditional Central Asian elements.
mosques.history: Built in 1999 after Kazakhstan's independence. Replaced older Soviet-era mosque. Expanded to meet growing congregation.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors outside prayer times. Located in central Almaty.

mosques.name: Mashkhur Jusup Mosque
mosques.significance: Distinctive eight-pointed star design, one of Kazakhstan's architectural landmarks
mosques.description: Mashkhur Jusup Mosque features a unique eight-pointed star floor plan, making it one of the most architecturally distinctive mosques in Central Asia. Named after the Kazakh poet and philosopher Mashkhur Jusup Kopeyev.
mosques.architectureNotes: Unique eight-pointed star plan. Golden dome. Named after poet Mashkhur Jusup Kopeyev (1858-1931).
mosques.history: Completed 2001. Named after Kazakh poet, philosopher, and ethnographer Mashkhur Jusup Kopeyev.
mosques.tourismNotes: Architectural attraction. Open to visitors. Located on the Irtysh River embankment.

mosques.name: Manjali Mosque
mosques.significance: Main mosque of western Kazakhstan's oil-rich Atyrau region
mosques.description: Manjali Mosque serves as the central Jumu'ah mosque for western Kazakhstan. Located in the oil hub of Atyrau, it combines modern construction with traditional Central Asian Islamic design elements.
mosques.architectureNotes: Blue dome, traditional Central Asian patterns. Serves the oil industry workers and local population.
mosques.history: Built 2001 to serve the growing population of Atyrau, Kazakhstan's oil capital on the Caspian Sea.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Atyrau is a major energy industry hub.

mosques.name: Türkmenbaşy Ruhy Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest mosques in Central Asia, mausoleum of Saparmurat Niyazov
mosques.description: Türkmenbaşy Ruhy Mosque is a monumental mosque-mausoleum complex near Ashgabat. Built of white marble with gold details, it houses the tomb of Turkmenistan's first president. Its four 91m minarets represent 1991, the year of independence.
mosques.architectureNotes: Four 91m minarets (representing 1991). White marble exterior. 50m golden dome. Houses presidential mausoleum.
mosques.history: Completed 2004 by President Saparmurat Niyazov in his home village. Designed as national symbol and presidential burial site.
mosques.tourismNotes: Tours available. Located 15km from Ashgabat in Gypjak village. Photography restrictions may apply.

mosques.name: Bibi-Khanym Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest and most ambitious mosques of the medieval Islamic world
mosques.description: Bibi-Khanym Mosque was built 1399-1404 under Timur (Tamerlane) as the grandest mosque of his empire. Named after his chief wife, it featured one of the largest domes ever attempted. Though partially ruined, its massive gateway and courtyard remain awe-inspiring.
mosques.architectureNotes: Monumental gateway (35m). 167×109m courtyard. Original dome collapsed. Restored 20th century. Blue tile work.
mosques.history: Built 1399-1404 by Timur using craftsmen from across his empire including those captured from Delhi. Dome collapsed due to ambitious scale. Major restoration in Soviet and post-Soviet periods.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO site. Part of Samarkand's historic center. Open daily. Best visited with Registan and Shah-i-Zinda.

mosques.name: Kalyan Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the largest Friday mosques in Central Asia, part of Po-i-Kalyan ensemble
mosques.description: Kalyan Mosque (Great Mosque) is part of the famous Po-i-Kalyan complex in Bukhara. Its courtyard is surrounded by 288 domed galleries supporting 208 columns. The adjacent Kalyan Minaret survived Genghis Khan's destruction of Bukhara.
mosques.architectureNotes: 130×80m courtyard. 288 domed galleries. 208 columns. Blue-tiled entrance portal. Adjacent to famous Kalyan Minaret (1127).
mosques.history: Current structure built 1514 under Shaybanid rule, replacing 12th-century mosque. Kalyan Minaret (1127) spared by Genghis Khan. Po-i-Kalyan means 'At the foot of the Great'.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO World Heritage. Active mosque. Best visited with Mir-i-Arab Madrasah opposite. Photography allowed.

mosques.name: Hazrat Imam Mosque
mosques.significance: Houses one of the world's oldest Quran manuscripts (Uthman Quran)
mosques.description: Hazrat Imam Mosque is part of Tashkent's main religious complex, the Khast Imam. The adjacent library houses the Uthman Quran, one of the oldest Quran manuscripts in existence, attributed to Caliph Uthman ibn Affan.
mosques.architectureNotes: Modern construction with traditional Uzbek patterns. Part of Khast Imam religious complex. Blue domes and white marble.
mosques.history: Current mosque built 2007 on historic Khast Imam site. Complex houses Muyi Mubarak Library with Uthman Quran (7th century).
mosques.tourismNotes: Uthman Quran viewable in library. Friday prayer popular. Central religious complex of Uzbekistan.

mosques.name: Minor Mosque
mosques.significance: Modern landmark mosque on Tashkent's Ankhor Canal
mosques.description: Minor Mosque is a striking white marble mosque completed in 2014 on the banks of Tashkent's Ankhor Canal. Its pure white exterior and elegant domes make it one of Uzbekistan's most photogenic modern mosques.
mosques.architectureNotes: White marble construction. Elegant domes and minarets. Waterfront location on Ankhor Canal. 2,400 indoor, 6,000 total capacity.
mosques.history: Completed October 2014. Named 'Minor' (white in Uzbek) for its white marble. Built on former industrial site.
mosques.tourismNotes: Popular for photography. Waterfront setting. Open to visitors outside prayer times.

mosques.name: Bolo Haouz Mosque
mosques.significance: Historic Friday mosque with distinctive 20-column iwan, facing the Ark citadel
mosques.description: Bolo Haouz Mosque ('Mosque by the Pool') is a historic Friday mosque opposite Bukhara's Ark citadel. Its stunning 20-column iwan with carved wooden columns and painted ceilings is one of Central Asia's finest examples of traditional craftsmanship.
mosques.architectureNotes: 20 carved walnut columns. Painted wooden ceiling (muqarnas). Reflecting pool. Faces Ark citadel.
mosques.history: Built 1712 for Emir of Bukhara. Iwan added 1917. Used by Emirs for Friday prayers. Pool once supplied city water.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO site. Active mosque. Best photographed with pool reflection. Opposite entrance to Ark citadel.

mosques.name: Uganda National Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Uganda and Sub-Saharan Africa
mosques.description: The Uganda National Mosque (formerly Gaddafi National Mosque) is the largest mosque in Sub-Saharan Africa. Commissioned by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, it accommodates up to 25,000 worshippers. Its 70m minaret offers panoramic 360° views of Kampala.
mosques.architectureNotes: 70m tall minaret. Twelve arches. Fusion of European, African and Arab-Islamic styles. Main dome over 50m. Chandeliers with Arabic calligraphy.
mosques.history: Construction began 1970s, delayed by political instability. Completed 2006, opened March 2008. Funded by Libya. Renamed 'Uganda National Mosque' in 2013 after Gaddafi's death.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Minaret climb offers best view of Kampala. Modest dress required. Located on Old Kampala Hill.

mosques.name: Kibuli Mosque
mosques.significance: Historic hilltop mosque and cultural landmark of Ugandan Islam
mosques.description: Kibuli Mosque sits on one of Kampala's seven hills and serves as the headquarters of the Uganda Muslim Supreme Council. The white-domed mosque overlooks downtown Kampala and holds deep historical significance for Uganda's Muslim community.
mosques.architectureNotes: White-washed exterior. Hilltop location. Views of Kampala.
mosques.history: Construction began late 1940s. Associated with Prince Badru Kakungulu, who helped spread Islam in Uganda. Headquarters of Uganda Muslim Supreme Council.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Hilltop offers city views. Part of Kampala's seven hills.

mosques.name: Jamia Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest and most prominent mosque in Kenya, marking 100 years in 2025
mosques.description: Jamia Mosque is Kenya's largest and most iconic mosque, located in the heart of Nairobi. Built between 1925-1933, it features distinctive silver domes and serves as the main Friday mosque for Kenya's capital. It celebrated its centenary in 2025.
mosques.architectureNotes: Silver domes. British colonial-era construction. Designed by William Landels. Indo-Islamic influences.
mosques.history: Foundation stone laid 1925. Completed 1933. One of East Africa's most significant Islamic architectural monuments. Marked centenary in 2025.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors outside prayer times. Located in central Nairobi near markets.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Kilwa
mosques.significance: Oldest standing mosque on the East African coast, UNESCO World Heritage Site
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Kilwa is the oldest surviving mosque on the East African coast, originally built in the 11th-12th century and expanded in the 14th-15th century. Part of the UNESCO-listed Kilwa Kisiwani ruins, it once featured the largest dome in East Africa.
mosques.architectureNotes: Coral stone construction. Domed and vaulted bays. Once largest dome in East Africa. Mihrab with carved coral.
mosques.history: Original structure 11th-12th century. Major expansion under Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman (14th century). Part of Kilwa Sultanate, major Indian Ocean trade hub. UNESCO World Heritage since 1981.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO site. Accessible by boat from Kilwa Masoko. Bring water. Best visited with guide.

mosques.name: Friday Mosque of Songo Mnara
mosques.significance: Important archaeological example of Swahili coastal Islamic architecture
mosques.description: The Friday Mosque of Songo Mnara is part of the UNESCO World Heritage ruins on Songo Mnara island near Kilwa. Dating to the 14th-15th century, it represents the refined Swahili stone town mosque architecture of the medieval period.
mosques.architectureNotes: Coral stone. Typical Swahili layout. Part of stone town complex.
mosques.history: Built 14th-15th century during height of Kilwa Sultanate trade. Abandoned after Portuguese disruption of trade routes. UNESCO World Heritage since 1981.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO site. Accessible by boat. Often visited with Kilwa Kisiwani.

mosques.name: Mosques of Harar Jugol
mosques.significance: Walled city with 82+ mosques, fourth holiest city of Islam according to some traditions
mosques.description: Harar Jugol, the historic walled city, contains over 82 mosques and 102 shrines, making it one of the holiest cities in the Islamic world. The city served as a major center of Islamic learning and trade, with some mosques dating to the 10th century.
mosques.architectureNotes: Aggregate entry for 82+ mosques. Traditional Harari architecture. Stone walls. Within UNESCO-listed walled city.
mosques.history: Mosques built from 10th century onwards. Harar was capital of Adal Sultanate, major Islamic learning center. City walls built 16th century. UNESCO World Heritage since 2006.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO site. Many mosques within walking distance inside walls. Hyena feeding tradition at night.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Asmara
mosques.significance: Most prominent mosque in Eritrea's capital, part of UNESCO-listed Asmara modernist heritage
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Asmara (Masjid Khulafa Al Rashideen) is the main congregational mosque of Eritrea's capital. Built in 1938 during Italian colonial rule, it features a distinctive minaret and is part of Asmara's UNESCO-listed modernist architectural heritage.
mosques.architectureNotes: Italian colonial-era construction. Rationalist architecture with Islamic elements. Part of Asmara's modernist heritage.
mosques.history: Built 1938 during Italian colonial period. Designed by Italian architects. Part of Asmara's UNESCO-listed modernist city (2017).
mosques.tourismNotes: Part of Asmara walking tours. UNESCO modernist city. Active mosque.

mosques.name: Abdülhamid II Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Djibouti, built by Turkey's Diyanet Foundation
mosques.description: Abdülhamid II Mosque is the largest mosque in Djibouti, built on land reclaimed from the sea. Constructed by Turkey's Diyanet Foundation and named after Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid II, it accommodates 6,000 worshippers and features a 27m dome and two 40m minarets.
mosques.architectureNotes: 27m dome. Two 40m minarets. Built on reclaimed land. Turkish Diyanet Foundation construction.
mosques.history: Construction began 2015. Opened 2019. Funded by Turkey as gift to Djibouti. Named after Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid II (r. 1876-1909).
mosques.tourismNotes: Modern mosque. Waterfront location. Open to visitors.

mosques.name: Mandhry Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the oldest mosques in Mombasa's Old Town on the Swahili Coast
mosques.description: Mandhry Mosque is one of the oldest mosques in Mombasa's historic Old Town. Built around 1570, it represents the traditional Swahili coral-stone mosque architecture with its simple undecorated style typical of the Swahili Coast.
mosques.architectureNotes: Coral stone construction. Simple undecorated Swahili style. No minaret (typical of old Swahili mosques).
mosques.history: Built c. 1570. One of oldest surviving mosques in Mombasa. Part of Old Town heritage area.
mosques.tourismNotes: Part of Mombasa Old Town walking tours. Active mosque. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Friday Mosque of Moroni
mosques.significance: Historic Friday mosque in Comoros capital, reflecting Swahili Coast Islamic heritage
mosques.description: The Friday Mosque of Moroni (Ancienne Mosquée du Vendredi) is the main congregational mosque of Comoros' capital. Dating to 1427, it reflects the islands' deep connection to Swahili Coast Islamic culture and Arab-African trading traditions.
mosques.architectureNotes: White-washed walls. Traditional minaret. Swahili Coast influences.
mosques.history: Original structure 1427. Comoros part of Swahili Coast cultural sphere. Arab and African influences.
mosques.tourismNotes: Central Moroni location. Active mosque. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Great Mosque of Kilwa Kisiwani
mosques.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; oldest standing mosque on the East African coast
mosques.description: The Great Mosque of Kilwa Kisiwani is the oldest standing mosque on the East African coast, dating to the 11th century. Built of coral stone, it was considerably enlarged in the 13th-15th centuries when Kilwa was a wealthy Swahili trading city controlling gold and ivory trade. The mosque is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
mosques.architectureNotes: Coral stone construction. Sixteen domed bays in main prayer hall. Persian influence. Flat roof sections with barrel vaulting.
mosques.history: Original mosque 11th century. Enlarged 13th-15th centuries during Kilwa's golden age. Ibn Battuta visited 1331. Portuguese arrived 1502. Declined after 16th century.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Boat access from Kilwa Masoko. Best visited with guide. Ruins only—not an active mosque.

mosques.name: Songo Mnara Mosque Complex
mosques.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; five historic mosques on one island
mosques.description: Songo Mnara contains the ruins of five mosques, a palace complex, and 33 domestic dwellings from the 14th-15th centuries. Part of the same UNESCO site as Kilwa Kisiwani, these ruins represent the height of Swahili trading civilization on the East African coast.
mosques.architectureNotes: Coral stone and wood construction. Enclosed walls. Domestic and religious architecture integrated.
mosques.history: Built 14th-15th centuries during Kilwa Sultanate's peak. Abandoned after 16th century decline. Archaeological excavations ongoing.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Accessible by boat. Ruins only. Best combined with Kilwa Kisiwani visit.

mosques.name: Harar Jami Mosque
mosques.significance: One of the oldest mosques in Africa; Harar is UNESCO World Heritage Site and fourth holiest city of Islam
mosques.description: The Jami Mosque is the main Friday mosque of Harar, a walled city in Ethiopia considered the fourth holiest city of Islam. Dating to the 10th century, it anchors a city with 82 mosques and three 10th-century mosques. Harar Jugol is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
mosques.architectureNotes: Simple whitewashed style. Twin minarets added 19th century. Blend of Ethiopian and Arab influences.
mosques.history: Founded 10th century. Harar became Islamic emirate. Walled city (Jugol) has 82 mosques. UNESCO inscribed 2006.
mosques.tourismNotes: Harar Jugol is UNESCO World Heritage. Famous for hyena feeding tradition. Modest dress required.

mosques.name: Cheraman Juma Masjid
mosques.significance: Oldest mosque in India; built during the lifetime of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
mosques.description: Cheraman Juma Masjid in Kodungallur, Kerala is India's oldest mosque, traditionally dated to 629 CE—built during the Prophet's lifetime. According to tradition, it was established by Malik ibn Dinar at the request of Cheraman Perumal, a Hindu king who converted to Islam. The mosque blends Islamic and Kerala architectural styles.
mosques.architectureNotes: Traditional Kerala architecture with Islamic elements. Wooden construction. Traditional oil lamp.
mosques.history: Built 629 CE by Malik ibn Dinar. Legend ties to Cheraman Perumal, last Chera king. Renovated multiple times. Original structure preserved.
mosques.tourismNotes: Heritage site. Welcomes visitors. Modest dress required. Near Kodungallur town.

mosques.name: Adina Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in South Asia when built; Bengal Sultanate masterpiece
mosques.description: Adina Mosque was the largest mosque in the Indian subcontinent when completed in 1375 under Sultan Sikandar Shah of the Bengal Sultanate. Its enormous prayer hall could hold thousands. Though now partially ruined, the surviving structure showcases Bengal's unique Islamic architectural tradition.
mosques.architectureNotes: Brick construction. 378 domes (originally). Pointed arches. Terracotta ornamentation. Hypostyle hall.
mosques.history: Built 1375 by Sultan Sikandar Shah. Modeled on Damascus Umayyad Mosque. Largest in South Asia at time. Declined after capital moved.
mosques.tourismNotes: Archaeological ruin. Open to visitors. Near Malda town.

mosques.name: Sixty Dome Mosque
mosques.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; largest historic mosque in Bangladesh
mosques.description: The Sixty Dome Mosque (Shait Gumbad Masjid) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the largest historical mosque in Bangladesh. Built in 1459 by Khan Jahan Ali, it actually has 77 domes (60 on the roof plus 11 unique chattris). The monument represents the golden age of Islamic architecture in Bengal.
mosques.architectureNotes: 77 domes total (60 on main roof). Terracotta decoration. Brick construction. Thick walls for cooling.
mosques.history: Built 1459 by Khan Jahan Ali. Bagerhat was major Muslim settlement. UNESCO inscribed 1985 as part of Historic Mosque City.
mosques.tourismNotes: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Near Khulna. Open to visitors. Active mosque.

mosques.name: Star Mosque
mosques.significance: Iconic Mughal-era mosque known for distinctive star motif decorations
mosques.description: Tara Masjid (Star Mosque) in Old Dhaka is famous for its intricate mosaic decoration featuring blue stars made from imported Chinese porcelain. Originally built in the 18th century, it was renovated in the early 20th century with the distinctive star patterns that give it its name.
mosques.architectureNotes: Blue and white star tiles. Imported Chinese porcelain. Decorative minarets. Five domes.
mosques.history: Built 18th century by Mirza Golam Pir. Major renovation early 20th century added star decoration. Chinese porcelain tiles.
mosques.tourismNotes: Old Dhaka landmark. Active mosque. Photography permitted outside.

mosques.name: Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque
mosques.significance: Iconic red and white striped mosque; landmark of Colombo and symbol of Sri Lankan Muslims
mosques.description: The Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque, also known as the Red Mosque, is one of the oldest mosques in Colombo and a major landmark with its striking red and white candy-striped pattern. Built in 1909, its unique Indo-Saracenic architecture makes it one of the most photographed buildings in Sri Lanka.
mosques.architectureNotes: Red and white striped exterior. Pomegranate-shaped domes. Indian and Moorish influences.
mosques.history: Built 1909 by Indian Muslim merchants. Used as landmark by ships entering Colombo harbour. Major renovation 2017.
mosques.tourismNotes: Major Colombo landmark. Welcomes visitors. Remove shoes. Modest dress. No photos during prayer.

mosques.name: Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque
mosques.significance: National mosque of Brunei; considered one of the most beautiful mosques in Asia-Pacific
mosques.description: The Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque is the national mosque of Brunei and a symbol of Islamic faith in the country. Named after the 28th Sultan, its golden dome, marble minarets, and artificial lagoon make it one of the most beautiful mosques in Asia-Pacific.
mosques.architectureNotes: Italian marble. Golden dome covered with 3+ million mosaic tiles. Stained glass. Escalators. Royal ceremonial barge in lagoon.
mosques.history: Completed 1958. Named after 28th Sultan (1950-1967). Italian architect Rudolfo Nolli. Marble from Italy, chandeliers from England, carpets from Saudi Arabia.
mosques.tourismNotes: Major Brunei landmark. Welcomes visitors outside prayer times. Dress code enforced. Robes available.

mosques.name: Jame' Asr Hassanil Bolkiah Mosque
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in Brunei; built to mark 25th year of Sultan's reign
mosques.description: Jame' Asr Hassanil Bolkiah is the largest mosque in Brunei, built in 1994 to commemorate the 25th anniversary of Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah's reign. With 29 golden domes symbolizing the 29th Sultan, it is nicknamed the 'Kiarong Mosque' after its location.
mosques.architectureNotes: 29 golden domes. Four minarets. Blue and gold color scheme. Modern facilities.
mosques.history: Completed 1994 for Sultan's Silver Jubilee. Named after current Sultan. Largest in Brunei.
mosques.tourismNotes: Open to visitors. Dress code enforced. Photography permitted. Near Gadong area.

mosques.name: Sheikh Karimul Makhdum Mosque
mosques.significance: Oldest mosque in the Philippines; dates to 1380
mosques.description: The Sheikh Karimul Makhdum Mosque on Simunul Island in Tawi-Tawi is the oldest mosque in the Philippines, dating to around 1380. It was founded by Arab missionary Sheikh Karimul Makhdum who brought Islam to the southern Philippines. The mosque contains pillars from the original structure.
mosques.architectureNotes: Four original pillars preserved. Rebuilt multiple times. White-washed walls.
mosques.history: Founded c. 1380 by Arab missionary. First mosque in Philippines. Islam predates Spanish colonialism by 200 years. Original pillars still standing.
mosques.tourismNotes: Remote location in Tawi-Tawi. Heritage site. Active mosque. Check travel advisories.

mosques.name: Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Masjid
mosques.significance: Largest mosque in the Philippines; gift from Brunei's Sultan
mosques.description: The Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Masjid, also known as the Grand Mosque of Cotabato, is the largest mosque in the Philippines and second largest in Southeast Asia. Funded by Brunei's Sultan, it opened in 2011 and serves the predominantly Muslim Bangsamoro region.
mosques.architectureNotes: Golden dome. Four minarets. Brunei-influenced design. Modern facilities.
mosques.history: Completed 2011. Funded by Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah. Largest in Philippines.
mosques.tourismNotes: Major Mindanao landmark. Welcomes visitors. Dress code required. Check travel advisories.
